methodologyNotes: Granularity: every lettered/roman-numbered sub-basket and exception in Article VI and every lettered clause of Sections 7.01 and 4.01 is its own unit; Articles III, V, VIII, IX, X and XI are captured at the section level with sub-clause units only where a clause carries independent operative effect (e.g. 9.02(b) sacred rights, 9.04(f)/(g), 10.01(a)/(b), 11.07(a)). In Article I only load-bearing definitions that gate capacity, ratios or entity applicability are enumerated; the remaining ~200 ordinary definitions are captured in one grouped unit, as is the benchmark-rate suite. Boilerplate sections receive one BOILERPLATE_SUMMARY unit each so no Article or Section is silently skipped.

units.description: Identifies this as the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated December 18, 2025 among Distribution Solutions Group, Inc. (f/k/a Lawson Products, Inc., the Company and Borrower Representative), Lawson Products, Inc. (IL), Baron Divestiture Company, Lawson Products Canada Inc. (BC), The Bolt Supply House Ltd. (AB), GS Operating, LLC and TestEquity LLC as Borrowers, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent. Recitals state the parties amend and restate the April 1, 2022 Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the 'Existing Credit Agreement') in its entirety, extend the revolver maturity, provide additional Term Loans and Revolving Commitments, and re-evidence (not novate) the existing Obligations.
units.notes: Establishes which document is operative today and that this supersedes the 2022 agreement as amended. Note there are five U.S. Borrowers and two Canadian Borrowers; the U.S./Canadian split drives the ring-fencing of obligations throughout.

units.description: EBITDA = Net Income plus twenty enumerated add-backs (a)(i)-(xx) (interest expense, taxes net of refunds, D&A, losses on permitted asset sales, non-cash losses, Closing Date Transaction Expenses paid within 180 days, non-recurring/unusual expenses, run-rate Cost Savings, Permitted Acquisition earn-out/purchase-price expenses, transaction fees, director fees, business-interruption insurance recoveries, amendment fees, indemnified fees, non-cash charges, Acquired EBITDA and 24-month projected acquisition cost savings, post-acquisition integration costs, equity-comp non-cash expense) minus six deductions (b)(i)-(vi). Add-backs under (a)(vii), (a)(viii) and (a)(xviii)(b) are together capped at 20% of EBITDA calculated before such add-backs (the 'Combined Cap').
units.notes: The single most load-bearing definition: EBITDA drives the Applicable Rate grid, both financial covenants in 6.12, and every 'Applicable EBITDA'-based basket. The 20% Combined Cap is the key limiter on synergy/add-back inflation.

units.description: Applicable EBITDA means EBITDA for the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries for the most recently ended four consecutive fiscal quarters for which financials were delivered under Section 5.01(a) or (b) (or, before the first such delivery, the Section 3.04(a) financials).
units.notes: This is the measure that grows the percentage-based baskets (15%, 25%, 15% of Applicable EBITDA) in Sections 6.01, 6.02, 6.04, 6.05 and the Available Amount.

units.description: Total Net Leverage Ratio = (Total Indebtedness minus Unrestricted Cash, with the cash netting capped at $100,000,000) divided by EBITDA for the four most recently ended fiscal quarters. Operating leases reflected on the balance sheet are excluded.
units.notes: Governs the 6.12(b) maintenance covenant, the Applicable Rate pricing grid, the Available Amount investment/Restricted Payment gates in 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv)/(v), and Permitted Acquisition condition (h).

units.description: Secured Net Leverage Ratio = (Total Indebtedness secured by a Lien on Loan Party assets minus Unrestricted Cash capped at $100,000,000) divided by four-quarter EBITDA; balance-sheet operating leases excluded.
units.notes: Sets the 4.00x incurrence test for junior-lien ratio debt under Section 6.01(q)(i)(B).

units.description: First Lien Net Leverage Ratio = (Total Indebtedness secured by the Administrative Agent's Lien securing the Secured Obligations plus Total Indebtedness secured by equal-priority Liens on the Collateral, minus Unrestricted Cash capped at $100,000,000) divided by four-quarter EBITDA; balance-sheet operating leases excluded.
units.notes: Sets the 3.75x incurrence test for pari passu secured ratio debt under Section 6.01(q)(i)(A).

units.description: Interest Coverage Ratio = EBITDA for a period of four consecutive fiscal quarters divided by Consolidated Interest Expense for that period.
units.notes: Denominator uses 'Consolidated Interest Expense'; a separately defined and nearly identical term 'Interest Expense' is used as the EBITDA add-back. Both are defined; the near-duplication is worth flagging.

units.description: Both terms mean total interest expense (including on Capital Lease Obligations) of the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries for the period on all outstanding Indebtedness, including LC and bankers' acceptance commissions/fees and net costs under interest-rate Swap Agreements, on a consolidated GAAP basis.
units.notes: Two substantively identical definitions exist; 'Consolidated Interest Expense' is the covenant denominator and 'Interest Expense' is the EBITDA add-back.

units.description: Total Indebtedness means the aggregate principal amount of all Indebtedness of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, but EXCLUDING clauses (i) (letters of credit / letters of guaranty as account party) and (m) (Swap Agreement obligations) of the definition of Indebtedness.
units.notes: The exclusion of undrawn/drawn LC obligations and swap mark-to-market from Total Indebtedness materially affects every leverage ratio calculation.

units.description: Thirteen-clause definition (a)-(m): borrowed money; bonds/debentures/notes; obligations bearing interest charges; conditional sale/title retention; earn-outs and deferred purchase price (excluding ordinary-course trade payables, unaccrued earn-outs, accrued expenses and current payables); debt secured by Liens on the person's property (capped at the lesser of the debt and the property's fair market value if not assumed); Guarantees; Capital Lease Obligations; LC/letter of guaranty reimbursement obligations; bankers' acceptances; Off-Balance Sheet Liabilities; Disqualified Stock; and Swap Agreement obligations.
units.notes: Gates Section 6.01 in its entirety; the earn-out carve-out in clause (e) is a meaningful exclusion for acquisition-heavy issuers.

units.description: Unrestricted Cash means unrestricted cash and Permitted Investments held by the Loan Parties on a consolidated basis, but only to the extent subject to account control agreements in favor of the Administrative Agent that grant it 'control'.
units.notes: Cash held by non-Loan-Party subsidiaries, or in accounts without a control agreement, does NOT count toward the $100,000,000 leverage-netting allowance.

units.description: The builder basket. Available Amount = (i) the greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA (pro forma) as of the last day of the most recent four-quarter period; plus (ii) net cash proceeds of Qualified Stock issuances after the Effective Date that are Not Otherwise Applied and not part of a Specified Equity Contribution; plus (iii) principal of post-Effective-Date Indebtedness exchanged or converted into Qualified Stock; plus (iv)-(vi) Returns, disposition proceeds and redesignation fair value from investments/Unrestricted Subsidiaries originally made using the Available Amount under 6.04(q) (each capped at the original investment); plus (vii) Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts; minus (viii) prior usage under Section 6.04(q) and Section 6.08(a)(iv).
units.notes: Shared resource: the SAME Available Amount is consumed by both Section 6.04(q) investments and Section 6.08(a)(iv) Restricted Payments; usage under either reduces capacity for the other. Clause (vii) recycles declined mandatory prepayment amounts into RP/investment capacity.

units.description: Five-category pricing grid keyed to the Total Net Leverage Ratio: Category 1 (>3.75x) ABR/Canadian Prime spread 1.75%, Term Benchmark/RFR spread 2.75%, commitment fee 0.35%; Category 2 (<=3.75x but >3.00x) 1.50%/2.50%/0.30%; Category 3 (<=3.00x but >2.25x) 1.00%/2.00%/0.25%; Category 4 (<=2.25x but >1.50x) 0.50%/1.50%/0.20%; Category 5 (<=1.50x) 0.00%/1.00%/0.15%. Category 2 applies until the first full-quarter Compliance Certificate after the Effective Date. Changes take effect three Business Days after delivery of financials/Compliance Certificate; failure to deliver puts pricing in Category 1 at the Administrative Agent's option or Required Lenders' request. A retroactive true-up applies if the financials or ratio calculation prove incorrect.
units.notes: Note Category 5 sets a 0.00% ABR spread, so ABR loans at the lowest leverage tier bear no margin.

units.description: Eleven cumulative conditions (a)-(k): not hostile/contested; same or related line of business; no Default before or pro forma after; 20 days' prior notice with draft documents and diligence package (including QofE) for acquisitions >= $50,000,000; must be made by a Borrower or Guarantor and structured as an asset purchase, merger into a Borrower/Guarantor, or purchase of substantially all voting Equity Interests; Loan Party must survive any merger; target must have positive pro forma adjusted EBITDA; pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 AND Total Net Leverage Ratio at least 0.25x inside the then-applicable 6.12(b) level; Section 5.13 collateral/guarantee actions taken; five Business Days' prior officer's certificate for acquisitions > $50,000,000; and aggregate consideration for acquisitions of Persons that do not become Loan Parties or assets that do not become Collateral capped at $87,500,000 over the term of the Agreement.
units.notes: Condition (k) is a hard lifetime cap on non-Loan-Party / non-Collateral acquisition consideration. Condition (h)(ii)'s 0.25x cushion is measured against the 6.12(b) level INCLUDING any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment.

units.description: Ten enumerated categories (a)-(j): tax Liens not yet due or contested; carriers'/warehousemen's/mechanics'/materialmen's Liens not overdue by more than 60 days or contested; workers' compensation and social security deposits; bid/trade contract/lease/surety/performance bond deposits; judgment Liens not constituting an Event of Default under 7.01(k); easements/zoning/rights-of-way; commodity/brokerage account margin deposits; contractual setoff rights (depository relations, pooled/sweep accounts, purchase orders); utility/municipal security deposits; and Governmental Authority Liens for Canadian Priority Payables not yet due or contested. Permitted Encumbrances may not secure Indebtedness except under clauses (d) and (e).
units.notes: Incorporated by reference into Section 6.02(b) and into Section 6.04(g) (deposits under clauses (c) and (d)).

units.description: Cash-equivalents definition: (a) U.S./Canadian federal government obligations maturing within one year; (b) highest-rated commercial paper maturing within 270 days; (c) CDs/BAs/time deposits/money market deposit accounts maturing within 180 days at U.S. or Canadian banks with capital and surplus of at least $500,000,000; (d) fully collateralized repos of not more than 30 days with such banks; and (e) AAA/Aaa Rule 2a-7 money market funds with at least $5,000,000,000 of portfolio assets.
units.notes: Also feeds the Unrestricted Cash definition and therefore the leverage-netting allowance.

units.description: MAE means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, operations or financial condition of the Borrowers and Restricted Subsidiaries taken as a whole; (b) any Loan Party's ability to perform its material Obligations; (c) the Collateral or the Administrative Agent's Liens on a material portion of the Collateral or their priority; or (d) the rights or benefits of the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank or Lenders under the Loan Documents.

Material Indebtedness means Indebtedness (other than Loans and Letters of Credit) or Swap Agreement obligations of the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries aggregating more than $50,000,000; Swap Agreement 'principal amount' is the net termination amount.
units.notes: Sets the trigger threshold for the cross-payment-default (7.01(f)) and cross-acceleration (7.01(g)) Events of Default, and for the Section 5.04 payment covenant.

units.description: Material Subsidiary means each Restricted Subsidiary (excluding non-U.S. and non-Canadian Subsidiaries) contributing more than 5% of EBITDA for the most recent four-quarter period or more than 5% of Consolidated Total Assets. If non-Material Subsidiaries in the aggregate exceed 10% of EBITDA or 10% of Consolidated Total Assets, the Company (or, after 10 days, the Administrative Agent) must designate additional Subsidiaries as Material Subsidiaries - first U.S. Subsidiaries, then Canadian Subsidiaries - to eliminate the excess.
units.notes: Determines who must become a Loan Guarantor and grantor under Section 5.13, and therefore who is bound by Articles VI and X.

units.description: Material Acquisition means any acquisition consummated after the Effective Date with aggregate total consideration in excess of $75,000,000.
units.notes: Gates the availability of the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment (leverage covenant step-up) in Section 6.12(b).

units.description: Change in Control occurs on (a) acquisition by any Person or group other than a Permitted Owner of Equity Interests representing more than 30% of the Company's ordinary voting power; (b) a majority of the Company's board seats occupied by persons who were not directors on the date of this Agreement nor nominated/appointed by the board or its appointees; or (c) the Company ceasing to own, free of Liens (other than Permitted Encumbrances and Liens securing the Secured Obligations), at least 100% of the outstanding voting Equity Interests of the other Borrowers. 'Permitted Owner' means any Person that, as of the Effective Date, owns more than 30% of the Company's voting power.
units.notes: Triggers the Event of Default in Section 7.01(m). The 'Permitted Owner' grandfather effectively exempts the existing >30% holder (LKCM Headwater and affiliates are the identified Affiliate Lenders).

units.description: Restricted Subsidiary means any Subsidiary other than an Unrestricted Subsidiary. Unrestricted Subsidiary means any Subsidiary designated as such on Schedule 3.14 as of the Effective Date or designated by the Company's board under Section 5.15 and not subsequently redesignated. 'Subsidiary' means any direct or indirect subsidiary of a Borrower or other Loan Party, and absent contrary language means a subsidiary of the Company.
units.notes: Entity-applicability driver: Article VI covenants bind Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries only; Unrestricted Subsidiaries fall outside the covenant perimeter but are subject to the 6.04(r) leakage cap.

units.sectionRef: 1.01 (Loan Party / U.S. Loan Party / Canadian Loan Party / U.S. and Canadian Secured Obligations)
units.description: The credit is bifurcated. U.S. Loan Parties are the U.S. Borrowers plus U.S. Subsidiary guarantors; Canadian Loan Parties are the Canadian Borrowers plus Canadian Subsidiary guarantors. U.S. Secured Obligations are the Obligations of U.S. Loan Parties plus their Banking Services and Swap Agreement Obligations; Canadian Secured Obligations are those of the Canadian Loan Parties and Foreign Subsidiaries. Canadian Secured Obligations expressly exclude U.S. Secured Obligations, and no Canadian Loan Party guarantees or secures the U.S. Secured Obligations.
units.notes: Central entity-applicability rule, reinforced in Sections 2.01 (last paragraph), 5.13(b) and (e)(i), 10.01(b) and 11.07(a). Canadian credit support flows one way only.

units.description: Obligations means all principal, LC Exposure, fees, expenses, reimbursements, indemnities and other liabilities of the Loan Parties under the Loan Documents, including post-petition interest and fees. Secured Obligations means all Obligations together with Banking Services Obligations and Swap Agreement Obligations owing to Lenders or their Affiliates, excluding Excluded Swap Obligations of any Loan Guarantor. Secured Parties include the Lenders, Administrative Agent, Issuing Banks, Banking Services providers, Swap counterparties, indemnitees and their successors.
units.notes: Cash-management and hedging exposures share the Collateral and the Article X guaranty; Section 2.22 notice determines their position in the 2.18(b) waterfall.

units.sectionRef: 1.01 (Revolving Commitment / Initial Term Loan Commitment / Maturity Dates)
units.description: Aggregate Revolving Commitments on the Effective Date are $400,000,000; aggregate Initial Term Loan Commitments are $700,000,000 (the Initial Term Loan Commitment includes re-evidencing existing Term Loans). Both the Revolving Credit Maturity Date and the Initial Term Loan Maturity Date are December 18, 2030 (next Business Day if not a Business Day). Issuing Bank Sublimit for JPMorgan is $25,000,000; the Swingline Commitment is $10,000,000 per the Commitment Schedule.
units.notes: Total facility size $1.1 billion with a five-year tenor. Commitment Schedule allocates across twelve lenders led by JPMorgan ($54.5M revolver / $95.5M term).

units.description: Prepayment Event means (a)(i) any Disposition made in reliance on Section 6.05(k), (ii) any Disposition of all or substantially all assets or Equity Interests of an Unrestricted Subsidiary, or (iii) any casualty, condemnation or eminent-domain taking; or (b) the incurrence of any Indebtedness by a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary that is NOT permitted under Section 6.01.
units.notes: Only 6.05(k) general-basket dispositions trigger mandatory prepayment - dispositions under the other 6.05 clauses do not. Clause (b) makes unpermitted debt incurrence a 100% mandatory-prepayment event (as well as a covenant breach).

units.description: Net Proceeds means cash proceeds of a Prepayment Event (including deferred proceeds as received, insurance proceeds and condemnation awards) minus (i) reasonable third-party fees and expenses, (ii) amounts required to repay Indebtedness secured by the disposed asset, and (iii) taxes paid or estimated payable and reserves for directly attributable contingent liabilities in the year of the event or the next year.

units.sectionRef: 1.01 (Limited Condition Acquisition / LCA Election / LCA Test Date)
units.description: A Limited Condition Acquisition is any Permitted Acquisition the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary is contractually committed to consummate without a financing condition, provided it closes within 120 days (plus up to 60 additional days solely for pending regulatory approvals) after signing. Specified LCA Representations are those acquisition-agreement representations material to the Lenders that give a termination right.
units.notes: Works with Section 1.06(b), which lets the Company test ratios, baskets and conditions at signing rather than closing.

units.sectionRef: 1.01 (Affiliate Lenders / Bona Fide Debt Fund / Debt Fund Affiliate / Affiliate Lender Cap)
units.description: Affiliate Lenders means LKCM Headwater Investments III, L.P. and its Affiliates (excluding the Company, its Subsidiaries and natural persons). A Debt Fund Affiliate is an LKCM affiliate that is a Bona Fide Debt Fund with information walls. The Affiliate Lender Cap (defined in Section 9.04(f)) is 20% of outstanding Term Loans for Affiliate Lenders other than Debt Fund Affiliates.
units.notes: Identifies the sponsor/large holder by name and permits sponsor debt buying subject to caps and voting disenfranchisement in Section 9.04(f).

units.description: Disqualified Institutions are Persons designated in writing by the Borrower Representative on or before the Effective Date as disqualified institutions or Competitors, plus name-identifiable Affiliates, plus post-closing supplements adding Competitors (effective two Business Days after delivery, non-retroactive). A Competitor is an operating company primarily engaged in substantially similar business operations. Bona Fide Debt Funds are excluded unless separately named.

Required Lenders means Lenders holding more than 50% of the sum of Aggregate Credit Exposure plus aggregate Unfunded Revolving Commitments (Unfunded Revolving Commitments deemed zero solely for acceleration votes), and after acceleration/termination, more than 50% of Aggregate Credit Exposure. Defaulting Lenders are disregarded and Affiliate Lenders are disregarded except as permitted by Section 9.04(f).

A Lender becomes a Defaulting Lender if it (a) fails within two Business Days to fund Loans, participations or other required amounts (absent a good-faith conditions-precedent objection); (b) publicly or in writing disclaims its funding obligations; (c) fails within three Business Days of request to certify that it will comply with its funding obligations; or (d) becomes subject to a Bankruptcy Event or Bail-In Action.

Detailed Dutch Auction mechanics for the Company or a Subsidiary to purchase Term Loans: Auction Notice specifying an Auction Amount of at least $5,000,000 in $1,000,000 increments and a Discount Range; Lender Return Bids in $1,000,000 increments with one bid per Lender; Applicable Discount determined as the highest Reply Discount that fills the Auction Amount, ratable allocation of Qualifying Bids, Failed Auction withdrawal right, and no withdrawal once initiated except a Failed Auction.
units.notes: Operationalizes the Section 9.04(f) Affiliate Lender assignments and Section 9.04(g) loan buybacks.

units.description: All-In Yield means the yield on Indebtedness in the form of interest rate, margin, OID, upfront fees or interest-rate floor, with OID and upfront fees equated to interest assuming a four-year life (or shorter remaining life), excluding arrangement, structuring and underwriting fees paid to arrangers.
units.notes: Feeds the 50 basis point MFN protection in Section 2.09(g) and, by cross-reference, Section 6.01(q)(iv).

units.description: Permitted Supply Chain Financing means one or more non-recourse supply chain financings on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent in respect of Supply Chain Financing Accounts, provided any sale is a true sale with recourse limited to breaches of representations, warranties or covenants regarding the sold accounts.
units.notes: Supports carve-outs in Sections 6.01(o), 6.02(o) and 6.05(j) - a receivables-monetization channel outside the general disposition basket.

units.description: An intercreditor, collateral trust or subordination agreement establishing relative Lien/claim priority whose terms are (i) consistent with market terms as determined in good faith by the Company and the Administrative Agent or (ii) reasonably acceptable to the Borrower and the Administrative Agent; modifications completed in accordance with Section 8.01(g) are deemed acceptable to the Administrative Agent.
units.notes: Required for secured or subordinated ratio debt under Section 6.01(q)(ii)(B) and the associated Liens under Section 6.02(p).

units.description: Disqualified Stock is equity that matures, is mandatorily redeemable, is putable at the holder's option, or converts into Indebtedness or other Disqualified Stock, in each case before the date 91 days after the latest Maturity Date, subject to customary change-of-control/IPO/asset-sale and management-equity carve-outs. Qualified Stock is any equity that is not Disqualified Stock.
units.notes: Disqualified Stock counts as Indebtedness under clause (l); Qualified Stock issuance proceeds build the Available Amount and fund the Section 7.03 Cure Right.

units.description: Payment in Full requires indefeasible cash payment of all Loans and LC Disbursements with interest, termination or 103% cash collateralization of Letters of Credit, payment of accrued fees and reimbursable expenses and other Secured Obligations (other than unasserted Unliquidated Obligations), termination of all Commitments, and termination of or satisfactory arrangements for Swap Agreement Obligations and Banking Services Obligations.
units.notes: Defines the endpoint of the Article V and VI covenants and of the Article X guaranty.

units.description: Specified Representations are the representations in Sections 3.01, 3.02, 3.03(b), 3.08, 3.12, 3.15, 3.17, 3.18 and 3.20 (organization, authorization, no law violation, Investment Company Act, solvency, security interest, margin regulations, use of proceeds, and anti-corruption/sanctions).
units.notes: The 'funds certain' subset for Limited Condition Acquisition financings under Sections 2.09(f) and 6.01(q)(vii).

units.sectionRef: 1.01 (Alternative Currency / Agreed Currency / Dollar Equivalent / Exchange Rate / Equivalent Amount)
units.description: Agreed Currency means dollars or an Alternative Currency; Alternative Currency means Canadian dollars plus any additional currency later agreed by the Borrower Representative, Revolving Lenders, Issuing Bank and Administrative Agent. Dollar Equivalent and Equivalent Amount are determined by the Administrative Agent using Reuters rates on the preceding Business Day, with fallback discretion.
units.notes: Adding an Alternative Currency requires unanimous Revolving Lender agreement, and amending the definition requires each Revolving Lender's consent under Section 9.02(b)(I).

units.description: Grouped summary of the interest-rate benchmark definitions: ABR/Alternate Base Rate (greatest of Prime, NYFRB + 0.50%, Adjusted Term SOFR one-month + 1.00%, with a 1.00% floor on ABR itself), Adjusted Term SOFR Rate, Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR, Adjusted Term CORRA Rate (Term CORRA + 0.29547% for one month / 0.32138% for three months), Adjusted Daily Simple CORRA (CORRA + 0.29547%), Canadian Prime Rate, Floor (zero), and the full Benchmark / Benchmark Replacement / Benchmark Transition Event / Benchmark Replacement Date / Available Tenor / Term CORRA Reelection Event apparatus.
units.notes: Mechanical rate plumbing; the only unusual point is the express 1.00% per annum floor on the Alternate Base Rate itself.

units.description: Grouped summary of the remaining roughly 200 defined terms in Section 1.01 that are cross-referential, procedural or purely descriptive (e.g. Account, Administrative Questionnaire, Affiliate, Bail-In terms, Beneficial Ownership Regulation, Business Day, Code, Collateral Documents, Environmental Laws, ERISA terms, FATCA, Governmental Authority, Hazardous Materials, IRS, Loan Documents, Person, PPSA, Register, Related Parties, Requirement of Law, Sanctions, Taxes, UCC, and defined terms whose meaning is 'has the meaning assigned in Section X'). None has independent operative effect beyond the sections that use them.
units.notes: Grouped deliberately; enumerating each would not add analytic value.

units.description: Loans and Borrowings may be classified by Class (Revolving, Initial Term, Swingline), by Type (ABR, Canadian Prime Rate, Term Benchmark, RFR) or by both.

Standard interpretive rules ('including' means without limitation, references to agreements as amended, etc.), plus (b) UCC/PPSA term equivalence (Illinois UCC terms fixed as of the date hereof; Article 8 references extended to Canadian securities transfer laws) and (c) an extensive Quebec civil-law translation table (hypothec, movable/immovable property, solidary liability, legal hypothecs, etc.).
units.notes: The Quebec and PPSA translation provisions are substantive for collateral enforcement in Canada, not pure boilerplate.

units.description: Accounting terms follow GAAP, with a negotiation right if GAAP changes (freezing the prior treatment until amended or the notice is withdrawn). Computations are made without giving effect to ASC 825-10-25 fair-value elections for debt and without ASC 470-20 convertible-debt bifurcation (debt always valued at full stated principal). Critically, ASU 2016-02 (Topic 842) lease accounting is frozen: any lease that would not have been a capital lease under GAAP as in effect on December 31, 2015 is not treated as a capital lease.
units.notes: The FAS 842 freeze keeps operating leases out of Indebtedness and therefore out of every leverage ratio - a material capacity driver.

units.description: Benchmark disclaimer: the Administrative Agent does not warrant the administration or performance of any interest rate benchmark or successor rate and has no liability for rate errors or for transactions affecting rate calculation.

(a) Acquisitions and out-of-ordinary-course Dispositions in the trailing four quarters, and any transaction requiring pro forma calculation, are given pro forma effect for the First Lien / Secured / Total Net Leverage Ratios and Interest Coverage Ratio using Regulation S-X Article 11 principles (as in effect prior to January 1, 2021) certified by a Financial Officer; pro forma financial-covenant tests use the Section 6.12 level for the quarter of consummation WITHOUT the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment (except when testing Permitted Acquisition conditions); and proceeds of Indebtedness incurred in the transaction may not be counted as Unrestricted Cash. (b) For a Limited Condition Acquisition the Company may make an LCA Election so ratios, baskets, representations and conditions are tested on the LCA Test Date (signing) rather than closing, with later ratio fluctuations disregarded; while an LCA Election is outstanding, other transactions are tested assuming the LCA has been consummated. The LCA Election does not apply to the Section 4.02 conditions for Revolving Loans or to a condition requiring absence of a specific Default at closing.
units.notes: Highly consequential for capacity conclusions: it fixes the measurement date for essentially every ratio-based basket in an acquisition context.

units.description: If any Loan Party issues Subordinated Indebtedness, it must cause the Secured Obligations to constitute senior indebtedness in respect of it; the Secured Obligations are designated 'senior indebtedness', 'designated senior indebtedness' and 'first lien obligations' for purposes of any such instrument and any Applicable Intercreditor Agreement.
Financial ratios are calculated to one decimal place more than expressed and rounded to the nearest number (rounding up if there is no nearest number).

In any Delaware-style division or plan of division, assets/liabilities transferred to a different Person are deemed transferred, and any new Person is deemed organized and acquired on its first date of existence by the holders of its Equity Interests.
units.notes: Anti-divisive-merger provision; works with the Section 6.03(b) prohibition on Divisions without Administrative Agent consent.

units.description: The Administrative Agent or Issuing Bank determines Dollar Equivalents of Alternative Currency Borrowings and Letters of Credit on each Revaluation Date; those Dollar Equivalents govern until the next Revaluation Date, except for financial statements and financial covenant calculations. Dollar-expressed minimums apply as Dollar Equivalents for Alternative Currency transactions.

On the Effective Date the Existing Credit Agreement (the April 1, 2022 Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, as amended) is amended, superseded and restated in its entirety by this Agreement, expressly WITHOUT novation: existing liens, indebtedness, obligations and guarantees are not paid, extinguished, released or discharged. Outstanding Loans and Obligations under the Existing Credit Agreement are re-evidenced under this Agreement. All references in the old Loan Documents to the Administrative Agent, Credit Agreement and Loan Documents are deemed to refer to this Agreement; old 'Commitments' continue as Revolving Commitments per the Commitment Schedule; old Revolving Loans continue as Revolving Loans; the Administrative Agent may make reallocations/deemed assignments without fees; notice periods and prepayment/commitment-reduction notices under the Existing Credit Agreement are waived. Each Loan Party ratifies and reaffirms all payment/performance obligations and all prior grants of liens and security interests, which continue to secure the Obligations.
units.notes: This is the version-control provision: it establishes that this December 18, 2025 document is the operative agreement, that the 2022 agreement is fully superseded, and that pre-existing collateral and guarantees carry forward without re-grant.

units.description: (a) Each Revolving Lender severally agrees to make Revolving Loans in dollars, Canadian dollars or another Alternative Currency during the Availability Period, subject to its Revolving Commitment and the aggregate Revolving Commitments; revolving borrowings may be repaid and reborrowed. (b) Each Initial Term Lender severally agrees to make its Initial Term Loan in dollars to the Company on the Effective Date; amounts prepaid or repaid on Initial Term Loans may not be reborrowed. Final unnumbered paragraph: notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no Canadian Loan Party is obligated to repay, support or guarantee any U.S. Secured Obligations or other obligations of a U.S. Loan Party, and payments by Canadian Loan Parties are applied only to Canadian Secured Obligations.
units.notes: The last paragraph is the operative Canadian ring-fence and is decisive for entity-applicability questions.

units.description: Borrowing mechanics: ratable funding by Class; several (not joint) Lender obligations; Dollar Revolving Borrowings must be all ABR or all Term Benchmark, Canadian Dollar Borrowings all Canadian Prime Rate or Term Benchmark, Term Loan Borrowings in dollars only; Swingline Loans are ABR dollar loans. Minimums: Term Benchmark, ABR and Canadian Prime Rate Borrowings in $100,000 multiples and at least $500,000; Swingline Loans in $50,000 multiples and at least $100,000. No more than twelve Term Benchmark and RFR Borrowings may be outstanding. No Interest Period may extend past the applicable Maturity Date.
units.notes: Section 2.02(a) states 'The Term Loans shall amortize as set forth in Section 2.11' but the amortization schedule is actually in Section 2.10(b) - an internal cross-reference error.

units.description: Borrowing Request timing and content: three Business Days for Term Benchmark Borrowings (one Business Day for Effective Date borrowings), same day by 10:00 a.m. Chicago for ABR/Canadian Prime Rate (9:00 a.m. for LC reimbursement financings); requests are irrevocable and signed by a Responsible Officer (signature waivable for Approved Borrower Portal submissions). Defaults: ABR if in Dollars, Canadian Prime Rate if in Canadian dollars, Dollars if no currency specified, one-month Interest Period if none specified. Borrowers may not request Dollar RFR Loans or Canadian Dollar RFR Loans before a CORRA Benchmark Transition Event.

Currency-of-payment indemnity: obligations denominated in a relevant currency are discharged only to the extent the payee can purchase that currency with the payment received; Borrowers indemnify shortfalls and the payee remits any excess (net of amounts shared under Section 2.18(d)).

The Swingline Lender (JPMorgan) may, but is not obligated to, make dollar Swingline Loans to the U.S. Borrowers only, subject to the Swingline Commitment ($10,000,000) and the Revolving Commitment limits; same-day request by 1:00 p.m. Chicago. The Swingline Lender may require Revolving Lenders to fund participations, which obligation is absolute and unconditional notwithstanding any Default or Commitment termination. Replacement and 30-day resignation mechanics.
units.notes: Swingline availability is discretionary ('may agree, but shall have no obligation') and is limited to U.S. Borrowers.

units.description: Letter of Credit facility: (a) issuance during the Availability Period with a cap of twenty outstanding Letters of Credit and Sanctions/legal-restriction issuance blocks; (b) aggregate LC Exposure may not exceed $25,000,000, and no Issuing Bank need exceed its Issuing Bank Sublimit (JPMorgan $25,000,000), though it may consider over-sublimit requests in good faith; (c) each LC expires the earlier of one year after issuance (or extension) and five Business Days before the Revolving Credit Maturity Date, with 103% cash collateral required for later-expiring LCs and for any LC outstanding at the Revolving Credit Maturity Date; (d) automatic Revolving Lender participations; (e) reimbursement by 11:00 a.m. with the option to finance via ABR/Canadian Prime/Swingline borrowing; (f) absolute and unconditional reimbursement obligations; (g) disbursement procedures; (h) interim interest; (i) Issuing Bank replacement/resignation; (j) cash collateralization at 103% of LC Exposure upon an Event of Default (automatic and immediate on a 7.01(h) or (i) event), held in the LC Collateral Account under the Administrative Agent's exclusive control, returned within three Business Days after cure or waiver; (k) Issuing Bank reporting; (l) LC Exposure determination including automatic-increase and post-expiry drawing rules; (m) LCs issued for Restricted Subsidiary account are Borrower obligations with guarantor defenses waived; (n) the Existing Letters of Credit on Schedule 1.01 are deemed issued under this Agreement.
units.notes: The $25,000,000 aggregate LC sublimit is a hard cap on letter-of-credit capacity within the $400,000,000 revolver.

units.description: Lenders fund by noon Chicago time to the Administrative Agent, which credits the Funding Account; customary Administrative Agent assumption-of-funding and clawback-with-interest provisions.

Conversion/continuation mechanics; irrevocable Interest Election Requests; no election of a non-conforming Interest Period, no cross-Class Type conversion, no currency change, and no election of Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR or Adjusted Daily Simple CORRA before the relevant benchmark transition. Absent a timely election a Term Benchmark Borrowing continues with a one-month Interest Period. While an Event of Default continues and the Required Lenders so direct, no Term Benchmark conversions/continuations are permitted and outstanding Term Benchmark/RFR Borrowings convert to ABR (Dollars) or Canadian Prime Rate (Canadian Dollars).

(a)-(d) Initial Term Loan Commitments terminate on funding or 5:00 p.m. on the Effective Date; Revolving Commitments terminate on the Revolving Credit Maturity Date; voluntary reductions in $1,000,000 multiples of at least $1,000,000 with three Business Days' notice, permanent and ratable, conditional termination notices revocable if tied to a replacement facility. (e)-(i) Incremental facility: the Borrowers may increase Revolving Commitments or add Incremental Term Loans, in minimum increments of $5,000,000, with aggregate post-Effective-Date incremental capacity capped at $500,000,000; Administrative Agent (and for revolver increases, Swingline Lender and Issuing Bank) approval of new lenders; conditions include reaffirmed representations, no Default (with a funds-certain construct for Limited Condition Acquisitions), and pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 assuming the increase is fully drawn. Incremental Term Loans rank pari passu, may not mature before the latest existing Maturity Date, may not shorten weighted average life, must be treated no more favorably than existing loans, and are subject to a 50 basis point MFN Provision that ratchets up existing Applicable Rates.
units.notes: The $500,000,000 incremental cap is a pure dollar cap with no incurrence-ratio alternative. Note Section 6.01(q)(iv) cross-references the MFN Provision as being in 'Section 2.09(l)', but 2.09 has no clause (l) - the MFN is in 2.09(g). Cross-reference defect.

units.description: (a) Revolving Loans due on the Revolving Credit Maturity Date; Swingline Loans due the earlier of that date and the fifth Business Day after funding, and all Swingline Loans must be repaid with the proceeds of any Revolving Loan. (b) Initial Term Loan amortization of $8,750,000 payable on the last day of each March, June, September and December commencing March 31, 2026 (as adjusted by Sections 2.11(e) and 2.18(b)), with the balance due on the Initial Term Loan Maturity Date. (c)-(g) Lender and Administrative Agent account records are prima facie evidence; promissory notes on request.
units.notes: $8,750,000 per quarter on a $700,000,000 term loan equals 5% per annum amortization.

units.description: (a) Voluntary prepayment at any time without premium or penalty, subject to notice and Section 2.16 breakage. (b) Mandatory revolver paydown/cash collateralization whenever the Dollar Equivalent of Aggregate Revolving Exposure exceeds the aggregate Revolving Commitments, with a 102% currency-fluctuation cushion and a two-consecutive-Business-Day outside limit. (c) Mandatory Term Loan prepayment of 100% of Net Proceeds of any Prepayment Event within three Business Days (asset/casualty events) or one Business Day (unpermitted Indebtedness), subject to (i) a $20,000,000 per-fiscal-year Asset Sale Prepayment Trigger threshold (only proceeds above the threshold must be applied) and (ii) a reinvestment right of twelve months, extended by 180 days if a binding commitment is entered into within twelve months. (d) Prepayment notice mechanics. (e) Mandatory prepayments apply ratably across Classes of Term Loans and within a Class first to accrued interest, then ratably to the first four scheduled amortization payments, then ratably to remaining installments. (f) Foreign Subsidiary repatriation relief where prohibited by law or adverse tax consequences, with no Default resulting. (g) Term Lenders may decline their share of mandatory prepayments by Rejection Notice; Declined Amounts are retained by the Borrowers as 'Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts'.
units.notes: Interaction worth flagging: Declined Amounts under 2.11(g) feed clause (vii) of the Available Amount, converting rejected prepayments into investment and Restricted Payment capacity. There is no Excess Cash Flow sweep in this facility.

units.description: Commitment fee at the Applicable Rate on the undrawn Revolving Commitment (LC Exposure counts as drawn; Swingline Exposure does not), payable on the fifteenth day after each quarter end and at Commitment termination, on a 360-day basis. LC participation fees at the Term Benchmark Applicable Rate on daily LC Exposure, plus separately agreed fronting fees and standard Issuing Bank charges. Separately agreed Administrative Agent fees. Fees are non-refundable.

(a)-(c) ABR/Canadian Prime Rate Loans bear the base rate plus the Applicable Rate; Term Benchmark Loans bear Adjusted Term SOFR or Adjusted Term CORRA plus the Applicable Rate; RFR Loans bear Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR or CORRA plus the Applicable Rate. (d) During the continuance of an Event of Default, the Administrative Agent or Required Lenders may impose a 2% per annum default rate on all Loans, on the Section 2.12(b) LC fees, and on other overdue amounts (revocable notwithstanding Section 9.02 'directly affected Lender' consent rules). (e) Interest payable in arrears on Interest Payment Dates. (f) 360-day year except Prime/CORRA/Canadian Prime computed on 365/366. (g)-(h) Interest Act (Canada) disclosure and Criminal Code (Canada) criminal-rate savings clause with reimbursement mechanics.
units.notes: The default rate is elective (not automatic) and applies at 2% over the otherwise applicable rate.

units.description: Full benchmark-transition machinery: (a) inability to ascertain or unfair-cost fallback, converting Term Benchmark to RFR or ABR (Dollars) or Canadian Prime Rate (Canadian dollars); (b) automatic Benchmark Replacement on a Benchmark Transition Event, with a five-Business-Day Required Lender negative-consent window for clause (2) replacements; (c) Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes without consent, and Term CORRA reelection on delivery of a Term CORRA Notice; (d) notice obligations and conclusive-determination rights; (e) removal and reinstatement of non-representative tenors; (f) Benchmark Unavailability Period conversions.

Customary increased-cost and capital-adequacy yield protection for Changes in Law, with conclusive-absent-manifest-error certificates, ten-day payment, and a 180-day lookback limitation (extended for retroactive Changes in Law). Dodd-Frank and Basel III are deemed Changes in Law regardless of enactment date.

Breakage indemnity for prepayment, conversion, failure to borrow/convert/continue/prepay, or assignment of Term Benchmark or term RFR Loans off an Interest Period or Interest Payment Date, and for failure to pay Alternative Currency amounts on the due date or in a different currency.

Standard tax gross-up regime: payments free of Taxes with gross-up for Indemnified Taxes; Other Taxes paid by Loan Parties; Loan Party and Lender indemnities; Lender documentation requirements (W-9, W-8BEN/BEN-E, W-8ECI, W-8IMY, U.S. Tax Compliance Certificates, FATCA); refund sharing; survival. Canadian-specific Excluded Taxes address Part XIII ITA non-arm's-length and specified-shareholder withholding.

(a) Payment mechanics and currency. (b) Application waterfall for Collateral proceeds and for all payments after an Event of Default when the Administrative Agent elects or the Required Lenders direct: first, Administrative Agent/Swingline Lender/Issuing Bank fees, indemnities and expenses; second, Lender fees, indemnities and expenses; third, accrued interest ratably; fourth, principal, unreimbursed LC Disbursements, 103% LC cash collateral, and Swap Agreement Obligations and Banking Services Obligations up to the amount last notified under Section 2.22, ratably; fifth, all other Secured Obligations. Amounts from a Loan Party are never applied to that party's Excluded Swap Obligations. Banking Services and Swap obligations drop to the fifth tier if the Administrative Agent has not received the Section 2.22 notice. (d) Pro rata sharing of setoffs through purchased participations. (e) Administrative Agent presumption of Borrower payment with clawback. (f) Account statements are a convenience and estimates only.
units.notes: The waterfall is a shared-resource provision: hedge and cash-management counterparties share fourth-tier recovery with principal, but only up to the last notified amount.

units.description: Lenders claiming increased costs or triggering tax gross-up must use reasonable efforts to redesignate a lending office; the Borrowers may require any such Lender, or any Defaulting Lender, to assign its interests at par plus accrued amounts, subject to Administrative Agent consent and the Section 9.04 restrictions, with Affiliate Lender assignees subject to Section 9.04(f).

Defaulting Lender regime: commitment fees cease to accrue; payments are applied through an eight-tier priority waterfall; the Defaulting Lender loses its vote and is excluded from Required Lender calculations; Swingline and LC Exposure is reallocated among non-Defaulting Lenders up to their Revolving Commitments and otherwise prepaid or cash collateralized; fee adjustments; and the Swingline Lender and Issuing Bank need not extend new credit unless 103% covered. Parallel protections apply where a Lender's Parent suffers a Bankruptcy Event or Bail-In Action or where the Swingline Lender/Issuing Bank believes a Lender has defaulted elsewhere. Cure and readjustment mechanics on remediation.

If any payment applied to the Obligations must be surrendered as a preference, fraudulent transfer, impermissible setoff or otherwise, the Obligations are revived and continued as if the payment had never been received; the provision survives termination of the Agreement.

Each Lender or Affiliate providing Banking Services or Swap Agreements to a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary must promptly notify the Administrative Agent of the aggregate amount of the resulting obligations and update it on significant change or request; the most recent information determines the waterfall tier under Section 2.18(b). JPMorgan and its Affiliates are exempt from this notice requirement while JPMorgan is Administrative Agent.
units.notes: Failure to give notice demotes those obligations from the fourth to the fifth tier of the 2.18(b) waterfall - a real recovery consequence.

units.description: Organization; Powers: each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, has requisite power, and is qualified where required except where failure could not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.
units.notes: A Specified Representation for funds-certain purposes.

units.description: Authorization; Enforceability: the Transactions are within each Loan Party's powers, duly authorized, and each Loan Document is a legal, valid and binding obligation subject to customary bankruptcy and equity qualifications.
units.notes: A Specified Representation.

units.description: Governmental Approvals; No Conflicts: the Transactions require no governmental consent except those obtained and perfection filings; will not violate any Requirement of Law; will not violate or cause a default under any binding indenture or agreement except where no Material Adverse Effect; and will not create any Lien on material assets other than Loan Document Liens.
units.notes: Clause (b) only is a Specified Representation.

units.description: Financial Condition; No Material Adverse Change: audited consolidated financials for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (reported on by Grant Thornton LLP) and unaudited financials for the fiscal quarter and year-to-date period ended September 30, 2025 have been furnished and present fairly in all material respects; and no Material Adverse Effect has occurred since December 31, 2024.
units.notes: The Section 3.04(a) financials are the fallback measurement base for every ratio and basket until the first post-closing delivery under Section 5.01.

units.description: Properties: Schedule 3.05 lists owned and leased real property; leases are valid and in effect absent Material Adverse Effect; good and indefeasible title or valid leasehold interests free of Liens other than those permitted by Section 6.02; ownership or license of all necessary intellectual property, with registered IP listed on Schedule 3.05.

Litigation and Environmental Matters: except for the Disclosed Matters (Schedule 3.06), no pending or threatened proceedings with a reasonable possibility of adverse determination that could reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect or that involve the Loan Documents; no material Environmental Liability claims; and no change in the status of Disclosed Matters resulting in or materially increasing the likelihood of a Material Adverse Effect.

Compliance with Laws and Agreements; No Default: compliance with all Requirements of Law and binding agreements except where failure could not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect, and no Default has occurred and is continuing.
Investment Company Status: no Loan Party or Subsidiary is an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
units.notes: A Specified Representation.

units.description: Taxes: all required returns filed and Taxes paid except contested amounts with adequate reserves or where failure could not have a Material Adverse Effect; no material tax liens filed or claims asserted.

ERISA: (a) no ERISA Event has occurred or is reasonably expected that could reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect, and Plan accumulated benefit obligations do not exceed Plan asset fair value. (b) As of the Effective Date none of the Canadian Pension Plans (listed on Schedule 3.10(b)) is a Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, and the Canadian Pension Plans are duly registered, properly administered and funded except where no Material Adverse Effect.
units.notes: Pairs with the Section 6.03(g) absolute prohibition on assuming Canadian defined benefit pension liability.

units.description: Disclosure: all material agreements and restrictions have been disclosed; written information furnished, taken as a whole, contains no material misstatement or omission, with the customary projections qualification; and the Beneficial Ownership Certification is true and correct in all respects as of the Effective Date.

Solvency: immediately after the Transactions and after each Loan and Letter of Credit, the Loan Parties taken as a whole satisfy the four standard solvency tests, and each Canadian Loan Party is not an 'Insolvent Person' under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada); no Loan Party intends to incur debts beyond its ability to pay.
units.notes: A Specified Representation; tested on a Loan-Parties-taken-as-a-whole basis rather than entity by entity.

units.description: Insurance: Schedule 3.13 describes all insurance maintained as of the Effective Date, premiums due are paid, and the coverage is believed adequate and customary.

Capitalization and Subsidiaries: Schedule 3.14 lists each Subsidiary and its relationship to the Borrowers, each Borrower's authorized equity classes and record/beneficial ownership, entity types, and whether each Subsidiary is a Loan Party, Material Subsidiary, Restricted Subsidiary or Unrestricted Subsidiary.
units.notes: Schedule 3.14 is the Effective Date designation of Unrestricted Subsidiaries and therefore fixes the initial covenant perimeter; it is also incorporated by reference as Schedule 6.04 existing investments.

units.description: Security Interest in Collateral: the Loan Documents create legal, valid, perfected and continuing Liens on all Collateral in favor of the Administrative Agent for the Secured Parties, having priority over all other Liens except Permitted Encumbrances entitled to statutory priority and Liens perfected only by possession the Administrative Agent does not hold, upon making UCC and PPSA filings and USPTO/Copyright Office/CIPO notices and delivering possessory collateral.
units.notes: A Specified Representation.

units.description: Employment Matters: as of the Effective Date no pending or threatened strikes, lockouts or slowdowns; wage and hour compliance except where no Material Adverse Effect; wages and benefits paid or accrued.

Margin Regulations: no Loan Party is engaged principally in purchasing or carrying Margin Stock; no proceeds used to buy or carry Margin Stock in violation of Regulation U or X; Margin Stock is not more than 25% of asset value.
units.notes: A Specified Representation.

units.description: Use of Proceeds: Loan proceeds have been and will be used as set forth in Section 5.08.
units.notes: A Specified Representation.

units.description: No Burdensome Restrictions: no Loan Party is subject to Burdensome Restrictions except those permitted under Section 6.10.

Anti-Corruption Laws and Sanctions: policies and procedures reasonably designed to promote compliance are maintained; the Loan Parties, Subsidiaries and their officers and directors (and to their knowledge employees and agents) are in material compliance and are not Sanctioned Persons; and no Borrowing, Letter of Credit or use of proceeds will violate Anti-Corruption Laws or Sanctions.
keyDefinedTerms: Canadian Economic Sanctions and Export Control Laws
units.notes: A Specified Representation.

units.description: Affected Financial Institutions: no Loan Party is an Affected Financial Institution.

Plan Assets; Prohibited Transactions: no Loan Party or Subsidiary holds 'plan assets' within the meaning of the Plan Asset Regulations, and the Transactions will not give rise to a non-exempt prohibited transaction under ERISA Section 406 or Code Section 4975.

Chapeau: the Lenders' obligation to make Loans and the Issuing Bank's obligation to issue Letters of Credit do not become effective until each of the conditions in Section 4.01(a)-(o) is satisfied or waived under Section 9.02; the Administrative Agent's notice of the Effective Date is conclusive and binding.
units.notes: The Effective Date is the operative date for the entire restatement; the definition of Effective Date points back to this Section.

units.description: Executed counterparts of this Agreement from each party, duly executed Loan Documents and requested certificates/instruments, requested promissory notes, and written legal opinions of U.S. and Canadian counsel satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.

Secretary's certificates for each Loan Party attaching authorizing resolutions, incumbency, charter documents certified by the applicable jurisdiction and bylaws/operating agreements, plus good standing certificates.

Closing certificate signed by a Financial Officer of each Borrower stating that no Default has occurred and is continuing and that the representations and warranties in the Loan Documents are true and correct as of the Effective Date.

Payment of all fees and invoiced expenses (invoices presented at least two Business Days before the Effective Date) and payment of all accrued and unpaid interest and fees owing to the Administrative Agent and Lenders under the Existing Credit Agreement, funded with proceeds of Loans made on the Effective Date.
units.notes: Confirms roll-over economics: the prior facility's accrued amounts are paid at closing rather than the facility being repaid and re-drawn.

units.description: Recent lien and intellectual property search results in each Loan Party's jurisdiction of organization and each jurisdiction where assets are located, revealing no Liens except those permitted by Section 6.02 or discharged at or before closing under satisfactory payoff documentation.
Notice designating the Borrowers' Funding Account to which Borrowing proceeds are transferred, together with a customary funding indemnification letter for any Term Benchmark Loan.
Solvency certificate signed by a Financial Officer of the Borrower Representative dated the Effective Date, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.
Delivery of certificates representing pledged Equity Interests with undated stock powers executed in blank, and pledged promissory notes and other possessory collateral endorsed in blank.
units.notes: Partially deferred: Schedule 5.14 item 4 allows delivery of originals within ten days after the Effective Date to the extent not already delivered.

units.description: All UCC financing statements, PPSA financing statements, federal intellectual property filings and other documents required to create a perfected first-priority Lien on the Collateral (subject to Liens permitted by Section 6.02) in proper form for filing, registration or recordation.
Evidence of insurance coverage satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and compliant with Section 5.10 and the Security Agreements.
units.notes: Deferred by Schedule 5.14 items 1 and 2 to 30 days after the Effective Date.

units.description: A properly completed letter of credit application if a Letter of Credit is to issue on the Effective Date, and execution of the Issuing Bank's master commercial letter of credit agreement.
Completion of all legal due diligence by the Administrative Agent and its counsel, the results of which must be satisfactory to the Administrative Agent in its SOLE DISCRETION.
units.notes: Unusually open-ended for a closing condition in a restatement; sole-discretion standard rather than reasonable satisfaction.

units.description: Delivery of audited FY2024 consolidated financials, unaudited Q3 2025 consolidated financials, projections through 2030 with assumptions, and a pro forma consolidated balance sheet and income statement for the twelve months ended September 30, 2025.

KYC/anti-money-laundering documentation including USA PATRIOT Act information at least five days before closing, IRS Forms W-8/W-9 for each Loan Party, and Beneficial Ownership Certifications for requesting Lenders (deemed satisfied on such Lender's signature).
Such other documents as the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank, any Lender or their counsel may reasonably request.

Each credit event requires that the representations and warranties in the Loan Documents be true and correct in all material respects (in all respects for representations qualified by materiality or Material Adverse Effect), with date-specific representations tested as of their specified date.

Each credit event requires that no Default have occurred and be continuing at the time of and immediately after giving effect to the Borrowing or LC issuance, amendment, renewal or extension. Each Borrowing and LC action is deemed a representation to that effect.
units.notes: Note the condition is 'no Default' (not merely no Event of Default), so an inchoate breach blocks new borrowings.

units.description: Notwithstanding failure to satisfy the Section 4.02(a) or (b) conditions, unless the Required Lenders direct otherwise, on the fifth Business Day after notice to the Lenders (absent a written Required Lender objection) the Administrative Agent may (but need not) continue to make Loans and an Issuing Bank may continue to issue, amend, renew or extend Letters of Credit for the ratable account and risk of the Lenders if the Administrative Agent believes doing so is in the Lenders' best interests.
units.notes: Non-standard agent-discretion override of conditions precedent - functions like a protective-advance right and could change conclusions about availability during a Default.

units.description: Until the Secured Obligations are Paid in Full, each Loan Party executing this Agreement covenants jointly and severally with all other Loan Parties for the benefit of the Lenders.
units.notes: Entity applicability: the affirmative covenants bind Loan Parties (and, where stated, Restricted Subsidiaries), not Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

units.description: Audited consolidated financial statements within 90 days after each fiscal year end (or earlier if the Form 10-K would be due, including automatic extensions), commencing with the fiscal year ending December 31, 2025, reported on by nationally recognized independent accountants without a going-concern or scope qualification.
units.notes: A going-concern qualification would itself breach this covenant; delivery under 5.01(a)/(b) is the measurement trigger for Applicable EBITDA, Applicable Rate and all ratio tests.

units.description: Unaudited consolidated quarterly financial statements within 45 days after each of the first three fiscal quarters (or earlier if the Form 10-Q would be due), commencing with the fiscal quarter ending March 31, 2026, certified by a Financial Officer.
units.notes: Note the first required quarterly delivery is Q1 2026 even though the first financial covenant test date is December 31, 2025.

units.description: A Compliance Certificate delivered concurrently with each annual and quarterly delivery, certifying fair presentation, stating whether a Default has occurred with details, setting forth reasonably detailed calculations demonstrating compliance with Section 6.12, and listing Restricted versus Unrestricted Subsidiaries whenever there have been changes.
units.notes: Exhibit D requires Schedule I calculation tables for both 6.12 covenants, Schedule II for the Applicable Rate category, and Schedule III listing Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

units.description: Annual budget/plan including projected consolidated balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement for each fiscal quarter of the upcoming fiscal year, delivered no later than 45 days after each fiscal year end, in form reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.

Additional information covenants: (e) SEC filings and shareholder materials promptly after public availability; (f) SEC investigation correspondence; (g) audit reports and management letters on request; (h) other information on request, including KYC/Beneficial Ownership information; (i) ERISA Section 101(k)(1)/101(l)(1) Multiemployer Plan documents on request; and (j) consolidating financial statements for the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries whenever Unrestricted Subsidiaries existed during the period. Documents filed with the SEC or posted to an accessible website are deemed delivered.
units.notes: Clause (j) is the mechanism by which Lenders can see the covenant-perimeter (Restricted Group) results separately from consolidated results.

units.description: Prompt written notice of: (a) any Default; (b) investigations, litigation or proceedings seeking damages reasonably expected to exceed $10,000,000, injunctive relief against material assets, claims against a Plan, material criminal misconduct, material environmental violations, tax or governmental charge liability over $10,000,000, or any material product recall; (c) material changes in accounting or financial reporting practices; (d) ERISA Events or Canadian Pension Events reasonably expected to result in aggregate liability exceeding $10,000,000; (e) any development resulting in or reasonably expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect; and (f) changes to the Beneficial Ownership Certification. Each notice must be in writing, bear a heading referencing 'Notice under Section 5.02 of Distribution Solutions Group, Inc. Credit Agreement dated as of December 18, 2025', and attach a Financial Officer's statement of detail and remedial action.
units.notes: Breach of 5.02(a) (Default notice) is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period; breach of the other clauses gets a five-day cure under 7.01(e)(i). Section 8.02(b) makes the specific heading a condition of deemed Administrative Agent knowledge.

units.description: Preserve legal existence and material rights, licenses, permits, franchises, governmental authorizations and intellectual property, maintain qualification to do business except where no Material Adverse Effect, and conduct business substantially in the same or reasonably related fields as of the date of this Agreement; mergers, amalgamations, consolidations, liquidations and dissolutions permitted under Section 6.03 are excepted.
units.notes: Breach of 5.03 with respect to a Loan Party's existence is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d).

units.description: Pay or discharge all Material Indebtedness and other material liabilities including Taxes that if unpaid could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect before delinquency, except good-faith contests with adequate GAAP reserves where non-payment pending contest could not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.
Keep and maintain all property material to the conduct of the business in good working order and condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted.

Keep proper books and records and permit representatives of the Administrative Agent or any Lender (including consultants, accountants, lawyers and appraisers) to visit, inspect, copy records and discuss affairs with officers and accountants on reasonable notice; absent a continuing Event of Default, no more than one visit or inspection per year. While an Event of Default continues, the Administrative Agent and Lenders may also conduct on-site field examinations of assets, liabilities and books and records, and the Administrative Agent may prepare and distribute Reports to the Lenders.
units.notes: Field examination rights are unlocked only by a continuing Event of Default; Section 9.03(a)(B) makes field exam costs reimbursable only during an Event of Default.

units.description: Comply with all Requirements of Law including Environmental Laws except where failure could not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect, and maintain and enforce policies and procedures reasonably designed to promote compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and applicable Sanctions.

(a) Initial Term Loan proceeds fund the Effective Date Transactions with the remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes; Revolving Loan, Swingline and Letter of Credit proceeds are used only for working capital and general corporate purposes of the Borrowers and Restricted Subsidiaries, expressly including the Effective Date Transactions, Permitted Acquisitions and Restricted Payments. No proceeds may be used in violation of Regulations T, U or X. (b) No Borrowing or Letter of Credit may be requested or used in furtherance of a violation of Anti-Corruption Laws, for dealings with Sanctioned Persons or in Sanctioned Countries in violation of Sanctions, or in any manner violating applicable Sanctions.
units.notes: Breach of Section 5.08 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period.

units.description: Ensure that information furnished to the Administrative Agent or Lenders, taken as a whole, contains no material misstatement or omission; furnishing information is deemed a representation to that effect; Projections need only be prepared in good faith on assumptions believed reasonable, with a full forward-looking-statement disclaimer.

Maintain with financially sound and reputable carriers insurance in customary amounts and against customary risks with no greater risk retention, plus all insurance required by the Collateral Documents; furnish detail on request but at least annually.

Blocking Statute Carve-Out: nothing in this Agreement requires a Canadian-incorporated Borrower carrying on business in Canada, or its directors/officers/managers, to contravene the Canadian Foreign Extraterritorial Measures Act or a similar Blocking Statute; if a Borrower would have to act contrary to that carve-out it must inform the Lenders and work in good faith to find a mutually acceptable mitigation before using credit proceeds.
units.notes: Materiality flagged uncertain because it partially qualifies the Sanctions covenants for Canadian entities. Also note a document defect: the Table of Contents lists Section 5.11 as 'Reserved', but the body contains this substantive Blocking Statute Carve-Out.

units.description: Furnish prompt written notice of any casualty or insured damage to a material portion of the Collateral or the commencement of eminent domain or condemnation proceedings, and ensure Net Proceeds are collected and applied in accordance with this Agreement and the Collateral Documents.
units.notes: Ties casualty and condemnation events into the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment machinery via clause (a)(iii) of Prepayment Event.

units.description: (a) Within 30 days after any Person becomes a U.S. or Canadian Subsidiary that is also a Material Subsidiary, or is designated a Material Subsidiary, the Company must cause it to deliver a Joinder Agreement and Security Agreement joinder with resolutions and, if requested, legal opinions; such Person automatically becomes a Loan Guarantor and grants Liens on its Collateral, excluding U.S. real property. Exception where a guarantee would create a material adverse tax consequence or the cost/burden outweighs the value. In no event may a Canadian Loan Party guarantee, support or provide Collateral for the U.S. Secured Obligations. (b) All owned property other than Excluded Property must be subject to first-priority perfected Liens, and 100% of the Equity Interests of directly owned Restricted Subsidiaries must be pledged, subject to the same tax/cost-benefit exception; Canadian Loan Party Liens secure only Canadian Secured Obligations. (c) Further assurances. (d) Post-acquisition material assets must be pledged on request. (e) Three overriding limitations: no U.S. Secured Obligations secured by Canadian Loan Party Collateral; no Collateral Documents or perfection actions required outside the U.S. and Canada; and the Administrative Agent may unilaterally waive perfection where the cost is disproportionate.
units.notes: This section, together with the Material Subsidiary definition, determines who is bound as a guarantor/grantor. There is no express foreign-subsidiary equity pledge limitation (e.g., no 65% CFC pledge cap), but clause (e)(ii) removes any obligation to perfect outside the U.S. and Canada.

units.description: The Loan Parties must take the actions listed on Schedule 5.14 by the dates specified (extendable by the Administrative Agent in its sole discretion): insurance evidence and lender loss payee/additional insured endorsements within 30 days; Deposit Account Control Agreements for each non-excluded Deposit Account within 60 days; delivery of original pledged certificates, stock powers and instruments within 10 days; commercially reasonable efforts within 30 days to obtain a release of NXT Capital, LLC's copyright security interest against TestEquity and to correct copyright chain-of-title records for six specified TestEquity/Jensen Tools copyrights.
units.notes: Breach of Section 5.14 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period, which makes these dated deliverables unusually consequential.

units.description: The Company may designate Restricted Subsidiaries as Unrestricted and vice versa, provided: no Default before or pro forma after and pro forma compliance with Section 6.12; no Loan Party may be designated Unrestricted; no Subsidiary may be designated Unrestricted if it would remain a 'Restricted Subsidiary' for other secured Indebtedness; an Unrestricted Subsidiary may not own Equity Interests or Indebtedness of, or hold a Lien on property of, a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary; an Unrestricted Subsidiary may not own intellectual property material to the business (non-exclusive ordinary-course licenses permitted if the Restricted Group retains beneficial ownership and equivalent use rights); and no Unrestricted Subsidiary Indebtedness may be guaranteed by or have recourse to any Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary or their property. Designation as Unrestricted is an investment under Section 6.04 at the date of designation; redesignation as Restricted is an incurrence of that Subsidiary's existing investments, Indebtedness and Liens and a return on the prior investment.
units.notes: Core anti-leakage architecture. Combined with Section 6.04(r)'s dedicated cap and the no-reallocation rule, the agreement tightly limits value transfer to Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

units.description: Until the Secured Obligations are Paid in Full, each Loan Party covenants jointly and severally with the Lenders; each negative covenant is framed as 'No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to ...'.
units.notes: Entity applicability: Article VI binds Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries. Unrestricted Subsidiaries are outside the perimeter, which is why Sections 5.15, 6.04(r) and 6.05 contain anti-leakage overlays.

units.description: General prohibition on creating, incurring, assuming or suffering to exist any Indebtedness, subject to the exceptions in clauses (a) through (r).
The Secured Obligations and the Guaranteed Obligations under this Agreement.

Intercompany Indebtedness of a Borrower owing to a Restricted Subsidiary and of a Restricted Subsidiary owing to a Borrower or another Restricted Subsidiary, provided (i) non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary debt owed to a Borrower/Loan Party is subject to Section 6.04, (ii) Loan Party debt owed to a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary must be subordinated to the Secured Obligations on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, and (iii) Indebtedness of Restricted Subsidiaries that are not U.S. Loan Parties owing to U.S. Loan Parties, together with Guarantees under 6.01(c)(iii) and investments under 6.04(b), may not at any time exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: SHARED BASKET: the 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap in 6.01(b)(iii) is a single aggregate cap shared with 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b). Usage under any one reduces capacity under the others.

units.description: Guarantees by a Borrower of Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness and by a Restricted Subsidiary of Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness, provided (i) the guaranteed Indebtedness is itself permitted by Section 6.01, (ii) Guarantees by Loan Parties of non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary debt are subject to Section 6.04, and (iii) Guarantees by U.S. Loan Parties of non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary debt, together with 6.01(b)(iii) Indebtedness and 6.04(b) investments, may not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: SHARED BASKET with 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.04(b).

units.description: Indebtedness owed to providers of workers' compensation, health, disability, other employee benefits or property/casualty/liability insurance pursuant to reimbursement or indemnification obligations, incurred in the ordinary course.
Loan Party obligations in respect of performance bonds, bid bonds, appeal bonds, surety bonds and similar obligations provided in the ordinary course of business.

Indebtedness existing on the date hereof and listed on Schedule 6.01, plus any Refinance Indebtedness in respect of it. Schedule 6.01 lists approximately $1,144,000 of Capital Lease Obligations and three acquisition indemnity escrow amounts ($1,275,000, CAD $5,000,000 and SGD 1,265,000).
units.notes: Grandfathered existing debt is small; the facility itself is essentially the entire capital structure.

units.description: Refinance Indebtedness extending, renewing, refinancing or replacing Indebtedness under clause (f) or clause (q), provided (i) no increase in principal other than unused commitments, accrued interest, fees, defeasance costs, premiums, discounts and expenses; (ii) securing Liens not extended to additional property; (iii) no additional obligors; (iv) no shortening of weighted average maturity; (v) terms not less favorable to the obligor; and (vi) subordination terms at least as favorable to the Administrative Agent and Lenders if the original was subordinated.

Indebtedness of any Person designated a Restricted Subsidiary after the date hereof, provided it exists at the time of designation and was not created in contemplation of it, capped at $20,000,000 outstanding at any time.
units.notes: Applies to redesignation of Unrestricted Subsidiaries as Restricted; note Section 5.15 treats redesignation as an incurrence of that Subsidiary's existing Indebtedness.

units.description: Customer deposits and advance payments (including progress payments) received in the ordinary course from customers for ordinary-course goods and services, to the extent constituting Indebtedness.

Indebtedness in respect of Banking Services, netting services, overdraft protection, employee credit card programs, automatic clearinghouse arrangements and similar deposit-account arrangements incurred in the ordinary course, and Indebtedness arising from a bank honoring a check drawn against insufficient funds in the ordinary course.
units.notes: Uncapped; Banking Services Obligations are also Secured Obligations sharing the Collateral and the 2.18(b) waterfall.

units.description: Obligations in respect of letters of support, guarantees or similar obligations issued for the benefit of the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary as required by law or in connection with statutory filings or audit opinions in non-U.S. jurisdictions, in the ordinary course.
Indebtedness consisting of insurance premium financing or take-or-pay obligations in supply arrangements, incurred in the ordinary course or consistent with past practice.
