Indebtedness of the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary incurred, assumed or issued in connection with any Permitted Acquisition, and Indebtedness of Persons acquired by or merged into the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary pursuant to a Permitted Acquisition.
units.notes: Uncapped in dollar terms - capacity is governed indirectly by the Permitted Acquisition conditions (including pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 plus the 0.25x cushion).

units.description: Indebtedness arising from agreements providing for customary indemnification, purchase price adjustments or similar obligations (including earn-outs) incurred or assumed in connection with a Permitted Acquisition, other permitted acquisition-type investment under Section 6.04, or Disposition permitted by Section 6.05.
Obligations under one or more Permitted Supply Chain Financings, to the extent constituting Indebtedness.
units.notes: Uncapped in this section; pairs with the Lien exception in 6.02(o) and the Disposition exception in 6.05(j).

units.description: Purchase money and capital-asset financing Indebtedness (including Capital Lease Obligations and assumed or pre-existing acquisition-asset debt) incurred to finance the acquisition, construction or improvement of fixed or capital assets, plus refinancings under clause (g), provided it is incurred within 180 days of the acquisition or completion and, together with related Refinance Indebtedness, does not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA outstanding at any time.
units.notes: Grows with EBITDA; corresponding Liens are permitted by Section 6.02(j). Note this 15% cap is separate from and additional to the 15% shared intercompany cap.

units.description: Ratio debt: other Indebtedness of a Loan Party that is unsecured or secured on a pari passu or junior Lien basis, subject to eight sets of conditions. (i) Incurrence tests: (A) pari passu secured requires pro forma First Lien Net Leverage Ratio not exceeding 3.75 to 1.00; (B) junior-lien secured requires pro forma Secured Net Leverage Ratio not exceeding 4.00 to 1.00; (C) unsecured requires pro forma compliance with the Section 6.12(b) Total Net Leverage Ratio covenant (including any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment). (ii) No such debt may be secured by non-Collateral assets, guaranteed by non-guarantors, or have non-Loan-Party obligors; secured or subordinated debt must be subject to an Applicable Intercreditor Agreement. (iii) Maturity no earlier than 91 days after the latest Maturity Date and no shorter weighted average life than the Initial Term Loans. (iv) Pari passu secured debt is subject to the MFN Provision. (v) Terms no more restrictive than the Initial Term Loans unless the Term Lenders receive the same benefit or the provisions apply only after the latest Maturity Date. (vi) Holders may participate pro rata or less than pro rata, never more, in Term Loan prepayments. (vii) No Event of Default at incurrence and bring-down of representations, with a funds-certain construct for Limited Condition Acquisitions. (viii) A Responsible Officer certificate delivered five Business Days in advance is conclusive absent Administrative Agent objection within that period.
units.notes: The principal incurrence-based debt capacity. Note the incurrence levels (3.75x first lien / 4.00x secured) sit at or below the 4.25x maintenance level, and clause (ii)(A)(3) bars non-Loan-Party obligors, closing the classic structural-subordination leak. Clause (iv) cross-references 'Section 2.09(l)' for the MFN Provision, but the MFN actually appears in Section 2.09(g).

units.description: General debt basket: other Indebtedness in an aggregate outstanding principal amount not exceeding the greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: The 'greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA' formulation recurs as a separate, non-shared basket in Sections 6.01(r), 6.02(q), 6.04(s), 6.05(k) and clause (i) of the Available Amount. Each is its own basket; only the Available Amount clause (i) is shared between 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv).

units.description: General negative pledge: no Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may create, incur, assume or permit to exist any Lien on any property or asset now owned or hereafter acquired, or assign or sell any income, revenues (including Accounts) or rights in respect thereof, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (q).
Liens created pursuant to any Loan Document.
Permitted Encumbrances (the ten categories defined in Section 1.01, which may not secure Indebtedness except under clauses (d) and (e) of that definition).

Liens existing on the date hereof and set forth on Schedule 6.02, provided they do not extend to other property and secure only the obligations they secured on the date hereof plus non-increasing extensions, renewals and replacements. Schedule 6.02 lists filings by Raymond Leasing, Citibank, Royal Bank of Canada, MUFG Union Bank, First-Citizens Bank & Trust and BNP Paribas Dublin Branch.

Liens existing on property before its acquisition, or on property of a Person before it becomes a Restricted Subsidiary (excluding redesignation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary), provided the Lien was not created in contemplation, does not extend to other property, and secures only pre-existing obligations plus non-increasing refinancings.

Collecting bank Liens under UCC Section 4-210 (or PPSA equivalent) covering only items being collected, and bankers' Liens and customary contractual setoff rights on deposit and securities accounts not given in connection with Indebtedness.
Liens arising out of Sale and Leaseback Transactions permitted by Section 6.06.
Liens granted by a Restricted Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party in favor of a Borrower or another Loan Party securing Indebtedness owed by that Restricted Subsidiary.

Liens in favor of customs and revenue authorities arising by law to secure customs duties on imports, and Liens on specific inventory or goods and proceeds securing bankers' acceptances or documentary letters of credit facilitating their purchase, shipment or storage, in the ordinary course.
Liens arising out of conditional sale, title retention, consignment or similar arrangements for the sale of goods in the ordinary course, not extending to other property.

Purchase money Liens on fixed or capital assets acquired, constructed or improved, provided they secure Indebtedness permitted by Section 6.01(p), are incurred within 180 days of the acquisition or completion, do not exceed the cost of the assets, and do not extend to other property.
units.notes: Sized indirectly by the 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap in Section 6.01(p).

units.description: Liens for workers' compensation, insurance and employee benefit legislation, good faith bid/tender/contract/lease deposits, public or statutory obligation Liens, cash or U.S. government bond deposits securing surety, stay, customs, performance or appeal bonds, rent deposits and warranty refund deposits, in each case in the ordinary course; plus Liens securing letters of credit, bankers acceptances or bank guaranties supporting those items.

Leases, franchises, grants, subleases, licenses, sublicenses, covenants not to sue, releases and consents (non-exclusive as to intellectual property) granted in the ordinary course that do not materially interfere with the business and do not secure Indebtedness.
units.notes: The non-exclusivity requirement for IP licenses is part of the agreement's IP anti-leakage architecture.

units.description: Liens arising from UCC or similar financing statement filings regarding operating leases or consignments entered into in the ordinary course.
Purported Liens (other than securing Indebtedness for borrowed money) incurred in the ordinary course and evidenced by precautionary UCC or similar public filings.
Liens on Accounts sold (or, on judicial recharacterization, granted as collateral) pursuant to any Permitted Supply Chain Financings.

Liens on the Collateral securing Indebtedness and other obligations permitted under Section 6.01(q)(i)(A) (pari passu) or (B) (junior), provided such Liens are subject to an Applicable Intercreditor Agreement having the required lien priority.
units.notes: The only route to sharing or subordinating the Collateral with third-party debt; sized by the Section 6.01(q) incurrence ratios.

units.description: General Lien basket: other Liens securing obligations in an aggregate principal amount at any time outstanding not exceeding the greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: Separate from, and stackable with, the 6.01(r) general debt basket.

units.description: No merger, consolidation, amalgamation, Disposition of all or substantially all assets or of all or substantially all stock of Restricted Subsidiaries, or liquidation or dissolution, except (if no Event of Default exists or would result): (i) a Canadian Subsidiary may merge into a Borrower with a Borrower surviving (and a U.S. Borrower must survive any transaction involving a U.S. Borrower); (ii) a U.S. Subsidiary may merge into a U.S. Borrower with the U.S. Borrower surviving; (iii) a Canadian Loan Party (other than a Borrower) may merge into another Loan Party with a Loan Party surviving (U.S. Loan Party must survive if a U.S. Loan Party is involved); (iv) a U.S. Loan Party (other than a Borrower) may merge into another U.S. Loan Party with a U.S. Loan Party surviving; and (v) a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary may liquidate or dissolve if the Borrowers determine in good faith it is in their best interests and not materially disadvantageous to the Lenders. Any merger involving a non-wholly-owned Restricted Subsidiary must also be permitted by Section 6.04.
units.notes: Note the directionality: Canadian entities may merge up into U.S. entities but the U.S. entity must survive, preserving the ring-fence and preventing U.S. assets from migrating into the Canadian silo.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may consummate a Division as the Dividing Person without the Administrative Agent's prior written consent; if a Loan Party LLC does divide, each Division Successor that is a Material Subsidiary must comply with Section 5.13 and become a Loan Party.
No engaging in any business other than businesses of the type conducted by the Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries on the date hereof and reasonably related businesses and reasonable extensions.
No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may change its fiscal year or any fiscal quarter from the basis in effect on the Effective Date.
units.notes: Prevents manipulation of the four-quarter measurement periods used in the financial covenants.

units.description: No Loan Party may change the accounting basis on which its financial statements are prepared except as required by GAAP or directed by the SEC.
No Loan Party will change the tax filing elections it has made under the Code.
units.notes: Drafted as an absolute prohibition with no materiality qualifier, reasonableness standard or consent mechanism - unusually rigid and worth flagging.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may contribute to, assume or cause an obligation to contribute to, or have any liability under, any Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, or acquire an interest in any Person that sponsors, maintains or contributes to (or did so within the preceding five years) a Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, without the Administrative Agent's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).
units.notes: A structural constraint on Canadian acquisition targets; interacts with the ERISA/Canadian Pension Event default in Section 7.01(l).

units.description: General prohibition on forming subsidiaries after the Effective Date, purchasing or holding Equity Interests, evidences of indebtedness or securities, making or permitting loans or advances, Guaranteeing obligations, making or permitting investments, or acquiring assets constituting a business unit, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (s).
Permitted Investments (the cash-equivalents categories defined in Section 1.01).

Investments by Loan Parties in Equity Interests of their Restricted Subsidiaries that are Loan Parties, provided such Equity Interests are pledged under the applicable Security Agreement; and provided further that the aggregate outstanding amount of investments by U.S. Loan Parties in Restricted Subsidiaries that are not U.S. Loan Parties made after the Effective Date, together with Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01(b)(iii) and Guarantees permitted under Section 6.01(c)(iii), may not at any time exceed 15% of EBITDA.
units.notes: SHARED BASKET with 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii). Drafting inconsistency worth flagging: this clause says '15% of EBITDA' while the two Section 6.01 counterparts say '15% of Applicable EBITDA'.

units.description: Loans and advances by a Loan Party to another Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, and by a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary to a Loan Party or other Restricted Subsidiary, provided loans by a Loan Party are evidenced by a promissory note pledged under the applicable Security Agreement, and loans and advances by U.S. Loan Parties to non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries are subject to Section 6.01(b)(iii) determined without regard to write-downs or write-offs.
units.notes: Also consumes the shared 15% cap; the 'without regard to write-downs or write-offs' language prevents impairment from freeing capacity.

units.description: Guarantees permitted under Section 6.01.
Notes payable, stock or other securities issued by account debtors to a Loan Party under negotiated settlements of Accounts in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.
Investments in the form of Swap Agreements permitted by Section 6.07.

Investments constituting deposits described in clauses (c) and (d) of the definition of Permitted Encumbrances (workers' compensation and social security deposits, and bid/trade contract/lease/surety/performance bond deposits).

Permitted Acquisitions, as defined in Section 1.01 with its eleven conditions including no Default, pro forma Section 6.12 compliance with a 0.25x cushion, positive target EBITDA, Loan Party acquirer/survivor, Section 5.13 collateral joinders, and the $87,500,000 lifetime cap on consideration for non-Loan-Party targets and non-Collateral assets.
units.notes: The principal acquisition channel; capacity is ratio-limited rather than dollar-limited except for the non-Loan-Party $87,500,000 sub-cap.

units.description: Investments of any Person existing at the time it becomes a Restricted Subsidiary (excluding redesignation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary) or consolidates or merges with a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, including via a Permitted Acquisition, so long as not made in contemplation of the transaction.
[Reserved].
units.notes: Note Section 6.05(d) cross-references 'investments permitted by clauses (g) and (j) of Section 6.04' even though clause (j) is reserved - a residual cross-reference from the prior agreement.

units.description: Investments existing on the date hereof and described on Schedule 6.04 (which incorporates Schedule 3.14 and adds one share of Columbus Insurance Ltd. for $36,000 and a 25% interest in JDJ Logistical Solutions, LLC for $560,000), plus modifications, replacements, renewals, refinancings, reinvestments and extensions that do not increase the investment amount other than per its terms plus accrued interest, premium, fees and expenses.

(i) Arms-length loans or advances (or Guarantees) by a Loan Party to employees in the ordinary course for travel and entertainment, relocation and similar purposes, capped at $5,000,000 outstanding at any one time; and (ii) non-cash loans to officers, directors, governors, managers and employees used simultaneously to purchase Qualified Stock of the Company.
Investments consisting of ordinary-course purchases and acquisitions of inventory, supplies, materials, equipment or similar assets, or of services.
Non-exclusive licensing of intellectual property in the ordinary course, or that does not materially interfere with the business and does not secure Indebtedness.
units.notes: Exclusive IP licensing is not permitted by this clause; see the 6.04 anti-leakage paragraph and Section 6.05's IP restriction.

units.description: Deposits required by any Governmental Authority or public utility, including for Taxes and similar charges, where the underlying obligation would not itself constitute an Event of Default.
Investments in prepaid expenses, negotiable instruments held for collection, and lease, utility, workers compensation, performance and similar deposits entered into in the ordinary course.

Available Amount investments: other investments up to the Available Amount immediately before the investment, provided that at the time and pro forma (i) no Event of Default exists or would result and (ii) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the ratio 0.50 to 1.00 lower than the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: draws on the same Available Amount as Restricted Payments under Section 6.08(a)(iv); clause (viii) of the Available Amount definition subtracts usage under both. Currently the leverage gate is 3.75x (4.25x less 0.50x).

units.description: Investments in Unrestricted Subsidiaries in an aggregate amount not to exceed the greater of $28,500,000 and 15% of Applicable EBITDA during the term of this Agreement.
units.notes: This is the ONLY channel for value transfer to Unrestricted Subsidiaries; the anti-leakage paragraph below makes it exclusive, non-replenishing and non-reallocable. It is a lifetime (term of the Agreement) cap, not an annual or outstanding-amount cap.

units.description: General investment basket: other investments, loans and advances in an aggregate outstanding amount not to exceed the greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA, measured when made, provided no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing or would result.

The amount of any investment is the amount actually invested without adjustment for later value changes, net of returns in respect thereof (dividends, interest, distributions, returns of principal, sale profits, repayments and income) not exceeding the amount initially invested.

For purposes of the Unrestricted Subsidiary definition, Section 5.15 and Section 6.04, 'investments' include the proportionate fair market value of a Subsidiary's net assets at the time it is designated an Unrestricted Subsidiary; on redesignation as Restricted, the Company is deemed to retain a permanent investment equal to the original investment less the proportionate fair market value of net assets at redesignation; and property transferred to or from an Unrestricted Subsidiary is valued at fair market value at the time of transfer.
units.notes: Prevents the classic trick of designating a subsidiary Unrestricted, dropping assets in, and redesignating it to reset investment capacity.

units.description: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may make investments in, transfer property to, or exclusively license property (including material intellectual property) to an Unrestricted Subsidiary other than pursuant to Section 6.04(r); (i) any such transaction permanently reduces the 6.04(r) basket, (ii) substantially contemporaneous cash returns do not replenish 6.04(r) capacity, and (iii) no other capacity under this Agreement may be reallocated to fund transfers to Unrestricted Subsidiaries.
units.notes: Explicit anti-J.Crew / anti-trapdoor provision: it forecloses reallocation of the general investment, disposition or Restricted Payment baskets to move assets outside the credit group.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may Dispose of any asset, including Equity Interests it owns, and no Restricted Subsidiary may issue additional Equity Interests (other than to another Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary in compliance with Section 6.04), except as permitted by clauses (a) through (k).

Dispositions of (i) inventory, goods or other assets in the ordinary course; (ii) obsolete, negligible, uneconomical, worn out or surplus property; (iii) assets no longer used or useful in the business; and (iv) other property (including leasehold interests) no longer economically practical in the business.
units.notes: Uncapped and not a Prepayment Event.

units.description: Dispositions of assets to any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, provided that dispositions involving a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary, or from a U.S. Loan Party to a Canadian Loan Party or vice versa, must comply with Section 6.09 (Transactions with Affiliates).
units.notes: The cross-silo U.S./Canadian transfer condition preserves the ring-fence by requiring arm's-length terms for cross-border asset movements.

units.description: Dispositions of Accounts (excluding factoring sales or dispositions) in connection with their compromise, settlement or collection.

Dispositions of cash and Permitted Investments and investments permitted by Section 6.04(g) and (j), Dispositions constituting Liens permitted by Section 6.02, and Dispositions constituting Restricted Payments permitted by Section 6.08.
units.notes: Cross-references Section 6.04(j), which is reserved.

units.description: (i) Sale and Leaseback Transactions permitted by Section 6.06; and (ii) Dispositions (including Sale and Leaseback Transactions) of real property or other fixed or capital assets acquired in the HISCO Acquisition, made for fair value, with aggregate fair market value not exceeding $20,000,000.
units.notes: A deal-specific carve-out for HISCO real estate; unlike 6.05(k), it does not trigger a Prepayment Event.

units.description: Dispositions resulting from any casualty, eminent domain taking, condemnation or similar proceeding affecting property of a Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary.
units.notes: Although permitted here, casualty and condemnation events are separately a Prepayment Event under clause (a)(iii) of that definition and trigger Section 2.11(c).

units.description: Foreclosures, condemnation, expropriation or similar actions on assets, Dispositions required by a Governmental Authority, and casualty or insured damage to assets.

Disposition or discount of inventory, accounts receivable or notes receivable in the ordinary course, and conversion of accounts receivable to notes receivable in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.

Leases, assignments, subleases, licenses, sublicenses, covenants not to sue, releases and consents (and terminations thereof) in the ordinary course that do not materially interfere with the business taken as a whole - expressly EXCLUDING any intellectual property.
units.notes: The express carve-out of intellectual property from this ordinary-course licensing exception is part of the IP anti-leakage design.

units.description: Dispositions resulting from sales of Accounts under Permitted Supply Chain Financings.

General disposition basket: Dispositions of assets, including Sale and Leaseback Transactions not permitted by clause (e)(ii), other than Equity Interests in a Borrower or in a Restricted Subsidiary (unless all Equity Interests in that Restricted Subsidiary are sold), capped at aggregate fair market value during any fiscal year of the greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA. Except as set forth on Schedule 6.05, all such Dispositions must be for fair value and at least 75% cash consideration.
units.notes: This is the ONLY disposition clause that triggers the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment (via clause (a)(i) of Prepayment Event), subject to the $20,000,000 annual Asset Sale Prepayment Trigger threshold and reinvestment rights. Note Schedule 6.05 is referenced but does not appear in the executed schedule set.

units.description: Notwithstanding the foregoing, no Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may consummate any transaction (by Restricted Payment, investment, Lien, sale, conveyance, transfer or other Disposition, in one or a series of transactions) resulting in the Disposition of intellectual property material to the business to any Unrestricted Subsidiary or any Restricted Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party; non-exclusive ordinary-course licenses are permitted so long as the Restricted Group retains beneficial ownership and equivalent use rights.
units.notes: Second and broader IP anti-leakage lock: it reaches non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries as well as Unrestricted Subsidiaries, and applies regardless of which basket is invoked.

units.description: No Sale and Leaseback Transactions except sales of fixed or capital assets that are (a) for cash consideration not less than the fair value of the asset and (b) consummated within 180 days after acquisition or completion of construction; condition (b) does not apply to Sale and Leaseback Transactions made in reliance on Section 6.05(e)(ii) or 6.05(k).
units.notes: Effectively limits sale-leasebacks to newly acquired/constructed assets unless run through the HISCO or general disposition baskets.

units.description: No Swap Agreements except (a) Swap Agreements entered into to hedge or mitigate risks to which a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary has actual exposure (excluding hedges of its own Equity Interests) and (b) interest-rate caps, collars or exchanges with respect to interest-bearing liabilities or investments.
units.notes: Non-speculative hedging only; Swap Agreement Obligations owing to Lenders or their Affiliates are Secured Obligations sharing the Collateral and the Article X guaranty.

units.description: General prohibition on declaring or making, agreeing to make, or incurring any contingent obligation to make, directly or indirectly, any Restricted Payment, subject to clauses (i) through (v).

Each Borrower may declare and pay dividends on its common stock payable solely in additional common stock, and on its preferred stock payable solely in additional preferred stock (to the extent issuable hereunder) or in common stock.
Restricted Subsidiaries may declare and pay dividends ratably with respect to their Equity Interests.
units.notes: Requires ratability, so minority holders cannot be favored over the Loan Party parent.

units.description: Loan Parties may make Restricted Payments pursuant to and in accordance with stock option plans or other benefit plans for management or employees of the Loan Parties and their Restricted Subsidiaries.
units.notes: Uncapped in dollar amount and not conditioned on absence of Default - unusually permissive for a management equity basket.

units.description: Available Amount Restricted Payments: other Restricted Payments up to the Available Amount immediately before the payment, so long as at the time and pro forma (x) no Event of Default exists or would result and (y) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the LESSER of (A) 2.50 to 1.00 and (B) the ratio 0.50 to 1.00 lower than the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: SHARED RESOURCE with Section 6.04(q): both draw on the single Available Amount and both are subtracted under clause (viii) of that definition. The RP gate is stricter than the investment gate because of the hard 2.50x ceiling.

units.description: General Restricted Payment basket: the Company may make other Restricted Payments up to $50,000,000 during any fiscal year, provided (x) no Default exists immediately before or after and (y) pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 WITHOUT giving effect to any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment. Any such Restricted Payment is excluded from the $50,000,000 annual cap entirely if, after giving pro forma effect, the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the lesser of 2.50 to 1.00 and the ratio 0.50 lower than the Section 6.12 maximum.
units.notes: Effectively an unlimited RP capacity below approximately 2.50x leverage, and $50,000,000 per year above it. Note the deliberate disallowance of the covenant step-up when testing pro forma compliance.

units.description: General prohibition on making or agreeing to make any payment or distribution of or in respect of principal or interest on any Indebtedness, or on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of any Indebtedness, subject to clauses (i) through (iv).
units.notes: Drafted broadly enough to capture all Indebtedness, not merely junior or subordinated debt, so any voluntary debt paydown must fit an exception.

units.description: Payment of Indebtedness created under the Loan Documents.

Payment of regularly scheduled interest and principal when due on Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01, other than payments on Subordinated Indebtedness prohibited by its subordination provisions or by any Applicable Intercreditor Agreement.
Refinancings of Indebtedness to the extent permitted by Section 6.01 (i.e., Refinance Indebtedness meeting the Section 6.01(g) conditions).
Payment of secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of a voluntary sale or transfer of the property or assets securing it, to the extent the sale or transfer is permitted by Section 6.05.
General prohibition on selling, leasing, transferring, purchasing or acquiring property or assets to or from, or otherwise transacting with, any Affiliate, subject to clauses (a) through (g).
Transactions that are both in the ordinary course of business and at prices and on terms not less favorable than could be obtained on an arm's-length basis from unrelated third parties.
units.notes: No dollar threshold and no independent-director or fairness-opinion requirement; the test is purely ordinary course plus arm's length.

units.description: Transactions (i) between or among the U.S. Loan Parties not involving any other Affiliate and (ii) between or among the Canadian Loan Parties not involving any other Affiliate.
units.notes: Note the intra-silo limitation: transactions BETWEEN a U.S. Loan Party and a Canadian Loan Party are NOT covered by this exception and must satisfy clause (a) (ordinary course and arm's length), as Section 6.05(b) confirms.

units.description: Any investment permitted by Sections 6.04(b), 6.04(c) or 6.04(d).
Any Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01(b) or 6.01(c).
Any Restricted Payment permitted by Section 6.08.

Payment of reasonable fees to non-employee directors of any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, and compensation, employee benefit arrangements and indemnities for directors, officers or employees in the ordinary course.

Issuances of securities or other payments, awards or grants in cash, securities or otherwise pursuant to, or the funding of, employment agreements, stock options and stock ownership plans approved by a Loan Party's board of directors.

No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may enter into, incur or permit to exist any agreement or arrangement prohibiting, restricting or conditioning (a) its ability to create, incur or permit Liens on its property in favor of the Administrative Agent to secure the Secured Obligations, or (b) any Restricted Subsidiary's ability to pay dividends or distributions on its Equity Interests, to make or repay loans or advances to a Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary, or to Guarantee Indebtedness of a Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary.
units.notes: Anti-negative-pledge and anti-dividend-blocker covenant; also underpins the Section 3.19 representation.

units.description: Restrictions and conditions imposed by applicable law or by any Loan Document.
Restrictions and conditions existing on the date hereof identified on Schedule 6.10, but not any extension, renewal, amendment or modification expanding their scope. Schedule 6.10 states 'None.'
units.notes: With Schedule 6.10 blank, there are no grandfathered restrictive agreements as of the Effective Date.

units.description: Customary restrictions and conditions in agreements relating to a pending sale of assets or of a Restricted Subsidiary, provided they apply only to the assets or Restricted Subsidiary being sold and the sale is permitted hereunder.

Clause (a) does not apply to restrictions imposed by agreements governing secured Indebtedness permitted by this Agreement if the restrictions apply only to the property or assets securing that Indebtedness.
Clause (a) does not apply to customary anti-assignment provisions in leases and other contracts.

Clause (b) does not apply to restrictions imposed by any agreement governing Indebtedness incurred after the Effective Date and permitted under Section 6.01(q) that, taken as a whole and in the Borrower's good faith judgment at the time of entry, are not materially more restrictive with respect to the Company or any Restricted Subsidiary than (x) customary market terms for that type of Indebtedness or (y) the restrictions in this Agreement.
units.notes: Permits ratio debt documents to contain their own subsidiary dividend/loan blockers, judged by a borrower-determined 'not materially more restrictive' standard.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may amend, modify or waive its rights under (a) any agreement relating to Subordinated Indebtedness, (b) any Original Restatement Date Acquisition Document (the Gexpro and TestEquity merger agreements), (c) the HISCO Acquisition Agreement, (d) documentation governing Indebtedness (other than the Secured Obligations) subject to an Applicable Intercreditor Agreement where the amendment is not expressly permitted by that intercreditor agreement, or (e) its organizational or governing documents, in each case to the extent the amendment, modification or waiver would be materially adverse to the Lenders.
units.notes: The 'materially adverse to the Lenders' qualifier appears to modify all five clauses, though its placement after clause (e) creates some ambiguity as to clause (d).

units.description: Minimum Interest Coverage Ratio: the Company will not permit the Interest Coverage Ratio (EBITDA divided by Consolidated Interest Expense) for any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters ending on the last day of any fiscal quarter, commencing with the fiscal quarter ending December 31, 2025, to be less than 2.75 to 1.00.
units.notes: Tested quarterly on a rolling four-quarter basis, first tested at December 31, 2025 (the quarter in which the Effective Date falls). Fixed level with no step-ups, step-downs or acquisition adjustment. Subject to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure.

units.description: Maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio: the Company will not permit the Total Net Leverage Ratio on the last day of any fiscal quarter ending on or after December 31, 2025 to exceed (i) 4.25 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after December 31, 2025 but prior to June 30, 2027, and (ii) 4.00 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after June 30, 2027. Upon written request of the Borrower Representative in connection with a Material Acquisition, the applicable maximum is increased by up to 0.50 to 1.00 for the four fiscal quarters ending immediately after the consummation date (a 'Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment'), available only twice during the term and only if no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, and never producing a level more than 0.50 above the unadjusted level. The Agreement is automatically amended to reflect an elected adjustment upon Administrative Agent notice to the Lenders.
units.notes: The single maintenance leverage covenant: 4.25x through the quarter ending March 31, 2027, stepping to 4.00x from the quarter ending June 30, 2027 through maturity, with up to two 0.50x acquisition holidays (so a maximum of 4.75x, or 4.50x after the step-down). Subject to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure. Several baskets test against this level with cushions: Permitted Acquisitions require 0.25x inside it; Sections 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv)/(v) require 0.50x inside it (and RPs also a hard 2.50x ceiling).

units.description: Chapeau: any of the events described in clauses (a) through (q) constitutes an 'Event of Default'.
Failure to pay principal of any Loan or any LC Disbursement reimbursement obligation when due, whether at maturity, on a prepayment date or otherwise. No grace period.
units.notes: One of the four 'hard' defaults (7.01(a), (b), (h), (i)) used as the funds-certain carve-out standard and the trigger for unrestricted assignment rights under Section 9.04(b).

units.description: Failure to pay interest on any Loan, or any fee or other amount payable under any Loan Document, when due, continuing unremedied for three Business Days.

Any representation or warranty made or deemed made by or on behalf of a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary in or in connection with any Loan Document, or in any report, certificate or financial statement furnished thereunder, proves to have been incorrect in any material respect (in all respects for representations qualified by materiality or Material Adverse Effect) when made or deemed made. No grace period.
units.notes: Because Compliance Certificates are 'deemed made' representations, a mis-calculated covenant certificate can be an immediate Event of Default.

units.description: Failure to observe or perform any covenant, condition or agreement contained in Section 5.02(a) (notice of Default), Section 5.03 with respect to a Loan Party's existence, Section 5.08 (use of proceeds), Section 5.14 (post-closing requirements) or ANY provision of Article VI. No notice requirement and no cure period.
units.notes: This is the covenant-breach default. Every negative covenant breach - including the Section 6.12 financial covenants - is an immediate Event of Default subject only to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure for 6.12. Notably Section 5.14 post-closing deliverables also carry no cure period.

units.description: Failure to observe or perform any other covenant in this Agreement or any other Loan Document, continuing unremedied for (i) 5 days after the earlier of a Loan Party's knowledge of the breach or notice from the Administrative Agent, if the breach relates to Section 5.01, Section 5.02 (other than 5.02(a)), Section 5.06 or Section 5.13; or (ii) 30 days after the earlier of knowledge or notice for any other Section of this Agreement or any other Loan Document.
units.notes: Two-tier cure periods; note the 5-day tier catches reporting (5.01), most notices (5.02), inspection rights (5.06) and additional collateral/guarantor joinders (5.13). Cure clocks run from knowledge, not just notice.

units.description: Cross-payment default: any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary fails to make any payment (principal or interest, regardless of amount) in respect of any Material Indebtedness when due. No grace period beyond that in the underlying instrument.
units.notes: Threshold is $50,000,000 aggregate via the Material Indebtedness definition; Swap Agreement termination exposure counts toward that threshold.

units.description: Cross-acceleration: any event or condition occurs that results in Material Indebtedness becoming due before scheduled maturity, or that enables or permits (after grace or cure periods) the holders or their agent to cause it to become due or to require prepayment, repurchase, redemption or defeasance before scheduled maturity; excluded is secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of a voluntary sale or transfer of the securing property permitted by Section 6.05.
units.notes: This is a cross-DEFAULT in substance ('enables or permits'), not merely cross-acceleration, and so is triggered by an unwaived covenant breach under any $50,000,000+ instrument even before acceleration occurs.

units.description: Involuntary insolvency: commencement of an involuntary case or proceeding, or filing of an involuntary petition (including a notice of intention), under any Insolvency Law seeking bankruptcy, liquidation, winding-up, dissolution or suspension of operations; composition, rescheduling, reorganization or other relief or stay in respect of a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary or its debts or assets; or appointment of a receiver, trustee, interim receiver, receiver and manager, liquidator, administrator, custodian, sequestrator or conservator, in each case continuing undismissed for 60 days or where an approving order or decree is entered.
units.notes: Applies to any Restricted Subsidiary, not just Loan Parties. A 7.01(h) or (i) event with respect to any BORROWER causes automatic acceleration and Commitment termination under Section 7.02(a) and is a CAM Exchange Date under Article XII.

units.description: Voluntary insolvency: any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary voluntarily commences a proceeding or files a petition under any Insolvency Law; consents to or fails timely to contest a Section 7.01(h) proceeding; applies for or consents to appointment of an insolvency official; files an answer admitting the material allegations of such a petition; makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or takes any action to effect the foregoing. No grace period.
units.notes: Automatic acceleration trigger with respect to any Borrower, and a CAM Exchange Date.

units.description: Any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary becomes unable, admits in writing its inability, or publicly declares its intention not to, or fails generally to, pay its debts as they become due, or any Canadian Loan Party becomes an 'insolvent person' under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).

Judgment default: one or more money judgments aggregating in excess of $50,000,000 (net of acknowledged insurance coverage) rendered against any Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary or combination thereof and remaining undischarged for 60 consecutive days without an effective stay of execution, or any judgment creditor legally acting to attach or levy on assets; or failure within 60 days to discharge non-monetary judgments or orders that could reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect, in each case where not stayed on appeal or appropriately contested in good faith.
units.notes: The $50,000,000 threshold also feeds back into the Permitted Encumbrances definition, which permits judgment Liens only for judgments that do not constitute a 7.01(k) Event of Default.

units.description: An ERISA Event or Canadian Pension Event occurs that, in the opinion of the Required Lenders, alone or together with all others, could reasonably be expected to result in aggregate liability of the Borrowers and Restricted Subsidiaries exceeding $50,000,000.
units.notes: Note the $50,000,000 default threshold versus the $10,000,000 notice threshold in Section 5.02(d).

units.description: A Change in Control shall occur (more than 30% acquisition by a non-Permitted Owner, majority board turnover, or the Company ceasing to own 100% of the voting Equity Interests of the other Borrowers free of Liens). No grace period.

Guaranty default: the Loan Guaranty fails to remain in full force and effect (other than per its terms), a Loan Party acts to discontinue it or asserts its invalidity or unenforceability, a Loan Guarantor fails to comply with its terms, or a Loan Guarantor denies further liability or gives notice to that effect.

Collateral default: except as permitted by the Collateral Documents, (i) any Collateral Document fails for any reason to create a valid security interest in the Collateral it purports to cover, or (ii) any Lien securing any Secured Obligation ceases to be a perfected first-priority Lien (other than Permitted Encumbrances).
units.notes: Interacts with Section 5.13(e)(iii), under which the Administrative Agent may unilaterally waive perfection where cost is disproportionate.

units.description: Any Collateral Document fails to remain in full force and effect (other than per its terms) or any action is taken to discontinue or assert the invalidity or unenforceability of any Collateral Document.

Any material provision of any Loan Document ceases for any reason to be valid, binding and enforceable in accordance with its terms, or any Loan Party challenges enforceability or asserts in writing or by conduct that any provision has ceased to be valid, binding and enforceable.

On any Event of Default other than a Section 7.01(h) or (i) event with respect to a Borrower, the Administrative Agent may (and at the Required Lenders' request shall) by notice to the Borrower Representative: terminate the Commitments including the Swingline Commitment; declare the Loans due and payable in whole or in part ratably across Classes, whereupon principal, accrued interest, all fees (including break funding payments) and all other Secured Obligations become immediately due without presentment or demand; require cash collateral for LC Exposure under Section 2.06(j); and exercise all other rights and remedies. On a Section 7.01(h) or (i) event with respect to any Borrower, the Commitments terminate automatically and all Loans, LC cash collateral obligations, interest, fees and other Secured Obligations become automatically due and payable without any notice. The Administrative Agent may also impose the default rate of interest.
units.notes: Automatic acceleration is limited to insolvency of a BORROWER (not any Restricted Subsidiary), even though 7.01(h)/(i) are triggered by any Restricted Subsidiary's insolvency.

units.description: Secured party remedies under the UCC, PPSA or other applicable law: collection, appropriation and realization on Collateral, consent to use of cash collateral, public or private sale, lease, assignment or credit bid, purchase by the Administrative Agent or Lenders free of redemption rights, assembly of Collateral at the Borrowers' expense, and application of net proceeds after costs in such order as the Administrative Agent elects; ten days' notice of sale is deemed commercially reasonable.

Equity Cure right: for purposes of determining whether a Default or Event of Default under Section 6.12 has occurred with respect to a fiscal quarter, at any time after quarter end until the tenth Business Day after the date financial statements are required to be delivered under Section 5.01(a) or (b) (the 'Cure Expiration Date'), the Company may issue Qualified Stock and apply the net cash proceeds (a 'Specified Equity Contribution') to increase EBITDA for that quarter, provided the proceeds are actually received as cash common equity by the Cure Expiration Date, are Not Otherwise Applied, and notice is given to the Administrative Agent on the date of receipt designating the amount.
units.notes: The cure is EBITDA-additive rather than debt-reducing, and the cure window extends ten Business Days past the financial statement due date.

units.description: Cure conditions: (i) no more than two Specified Equity Contributions in any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters; (ii) no more than five in the aggregate over the term of this Agreement; (iii) the amount is limited to what is required for pro forma compliance with Section 6.12; (iv) no pro forma reduction of Indebtedness (including by netting) with the proceeds for the cured quarter; (v) Specified Equity Contributions count toward EBITDA solely for Section 6.12 compliance and are disregarded for pricing, all other financial-ratio-based conditions, pro forma basket tests, the Available Amount and all baskets; and (vi) after notice of an intent to cure, no Loans need be made and no Letters of Credit need be issued, amended or extended until the contribution is made.
units.notes: Condition (v) is important: cure equity does NOT increase Applicable EBITDA for basket sizing or improve the Applicable Rate. Condition (iv) blocks 'over-cure' by prohibiting debt paydown netting.

units.description: Effect of cure: upon receipt of a Specified Equity Contribution before the Cure Expiration Date, Section 6.12 is deemed satisfied for that fiscal quarter as though there had been no failure, and any Default arising from that failure (and any Default arising solely as a result) is deemed not to have occurred for any purpose under the Loan Documents. Following notice of an intent to cure, and unless the Company notifies the Administrative Agent that it will not cure, neither the Administrative Agent nor any Lender may exercise any rights or remedies under Section 7.02 or otherwise based solely on a Section 6.12 failure until the failure is not cured by the Cure Expiration Date.
units.notes: This is a true standstill: it blocks acceleration and remedies for financial-covenant breach during the cure window.

units.description: Authorization and Action: appointment of JPMorgan as administrative and collateral agent with delegated powers and powers of attorney for non-U.S. Collateral Documents; the Administrative Agent acts on Required Lender instructions and need not act where it believes it faces liability without indemnity or where action would be contrary to law; no fiduciary duties; sub-agent appointment with limited liability; Arrangers and Co-Syndication Agents have no duties but receive indemnities; insolvency proof-of-claim powers; and, at clause (g), express Lender authorization and instruction for the Administrative Agent to enter into subordination and intercreditor agreements (including Applicable Intercreditor Agreements) with immaterial changes freely and material changes on five Business Days' negative-consent notice to the Lenders.
units.notes: Clause (g) is not boilerplate: it lets the Administrative Agent bind the Lenders to intercreditor terms (including junior-lien arrangements) on a five-Business-Day negative consent, complementing Sections 6.01(q) and 6.02(p).

units.description: Administrative Agent's Reliance, Indemnification, Etc.: exculpation absent gross negligence or willful misconduct (with a presumption of absence); no responsibility for recitals or Loan Party representations; deemed knowledge of Section 5.02 events and of Defaults only upon specifically labeled written notice; no duty to inquire into covenant performance, condition satisfaction or Lien perfection; reliance on counsel, notices and electronic communications; and no duty to monitor Disqualified Institution compliance.
units.notes: The deemed-knowledge rule ties back to the specific notice heading required by Section 5.02.

units.description: Posting of Communications: Approved Electronic Platform (IntraLinks, DebtDomain, SyndTrak, ClearPar or similar) may be used for Communications; acknowledgement of security risks; all-caps 'AS IS' disclaimer and limitation of liability for the Applicable Parties; notice of posting constitutes effective delivery; storage and alternative-notice preservation.

The Administrative Agent Individually: JPMorgan has the same rights and obligations as any other Lender or Issuing Bank in respect of its own Commitment, Loans and Letters of Credit and may engage in any banking or other business with the Loan Parties without accounting to the Lenders.

Successor Administrative Agent: 30 days' resignation notice; Required Lenders appoint a successor, failing which the retiring agent may appoint a U.S.-office bank; Borrower Representative approval required (not unreasonably withheld, and not required during a continuing Event of Default). If no successor accepts within 30 days the retiring agent may make its resignation effective, in which case it retains collateral-agent security interests solely for perfection purposes until a successor is appointed, the Required Lenders succeed to the agency role, payments go directly to the entitled Persons, and notices go to each Lender.

Acknowledgements of Lenders and Issuing Banks: commercial-loan (not securities) representations and independent credit analysis; deemed approval of closing deliverables; a full erroneous-payment ('Nium/Revlon') regime requiring return of erroneously transmitted Payments within one Business Day with interest, waiving discharge-for-value defenses, with Administrative Agent subrogation and non-satisfaction of Obligations, surviving termination; Report confidentiality and indemnity; and acknowledgement of information flow between JPMorgan and the Loan Parties with no agent duty to share.
units.notes: The erroneous-payment provisions are substantive lender-side obligations rather than pure boilerplate.

units.description: Collateral Matters: except for setoff rights under Section 9.08 and proofs of claim, no Secured Party may individually realize on Collateral or enforce any Guarantee - all powers are exercised solely by the Administrative Agent as 'representative' under the UCC; Banking Services and Swap Agreement counterparties get no Collateral management or release rights and are deemed to appoint the Administrative Agent and be bound as Secured Parties; and the Administrative Agent has no duty to ascertain Collateral value, existence, priority or perfection.
units.notes: Establishes exclusive agent enforcement and confirms that hedge/cash-management providers are passive Secured Parties.

units.description: Credit Bidding: the Secured Parties irrevocably authorize the Administrative Agent, at the Required Lenders' direction, to credit bid all or any portion of the Secured Obligations (including by accepting Collateral in satisfaction) at Bankruptcy Code Section 363/1123/1129 sales or other foreclosure sales, with acquisition vehicle formation, deemed ratable assignment of credit-bid Secured Obligations, governance by Required Lender vote, ratable issuance of equity or debt instruments, and automatic reassignment of unused Secured Obligations.

Certain ERISA Matters: each Lender represents and covenants to the Administrative Agent, Arrangers and Co-Syndication Agents that it is not using Benefit Plan 'plan assets', or that a PTE (84-14, 95-60, 90-1, 91-38 or 96-23) applies, or that it is a QPAM-managed fund, or another agreed representation; plus the standard no-fiduciary disclosure.

Flood Laws: JPMorgan will post flood-related documents it receives, but each federally regulated Lender and Participant is responsible for its own compliance with the National Flood Insurance Reform Act of 1994 and related legislation.

Quebec Security: each Lender appoints the Administrative Agent as hypothecary representative under article 2692 of the Civil Code of Quebec to hold any Quebec hypothec securing the Obligations and to exercise the rights and duties of a hypothecary representative, with power to delegate; successors and new Lenders are deemed to ratify the appointment, and the Administrative Agent has the same rights, immunities and indemnities in that capacity.
units.notes: Substantive Quebec collateral-perfection provision, not boilerplate, for a group with Canadian Loan Parties.

units.description: Borrower Communications: the Borrowers may (but need not) deliver Borrowing Requests, Interest Election Requests, prepayment notices, LC requests and other Borrower Communications through the Approved Borrower Portal, subject to acknowledged security risks, an all-caps 'AS IS' disclaimer, optional storage, and preservation of alternative notice methods.

Notices: addresses for the Loan Parties c/o the Borrower Representative at 8770 W. Bryn Mawr Ave., Suite 900, Chicago, IL 60631 (Attn: Ron Knutson, CFO) with a copy to Mayer Brown LLP; for the Administrative Agent, Swingline Lender, Issuing Bank and collateral agent at JPMorgan, 131 S Dearborn St, Floor 04, Chicago; and for other Lenders per their Administrative Questionnaires. Delivery, email and electronic platform effectiveness rules; addresses may be changed by notice. Certain personal contact details are redacted in the filed exhibit.

No failure or delay operates as a waiver; rights are cumulative; waivers are effective only if permitted by 9.02(b) and only for the specific instance; making a Loan or issuing a Letter of Credit is not a waiver of any Default even if known.

Amendments require the Borrowers and the Required Lenders (or, for other Loan Documents, the Administrative Agent and the affected Loan Parties with Required Lender consent). Sacred rights requiring higher consent: (A) commitment increases (that Lender); (B) reduction or forgiveness of principal, LC Disbursements, interest rate, interest or fees (each directly affected Lender) - with an express carve-out that amending the financial covenants or the defined terms used in them does NOT count as reducing interest or fees; (C) postponement of any scheduled payment date or Commitment expiration or reduction/waiver of any such payment (each directly affected Lender), other than Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayments; (D) changes to the ratable reduction of Commitments or the Section 2.18(b)/(d) payment application and sharing provisions (each Lender other than Defaulting and Affiliate Lenders); (E) changes to this Section or the Required Lenders definition or any voting-percentage provision (each directly affected Lender other than Defaulting and Affiliate Lenders); (F) changes to Section 2.20 (each Lender other than Defaulting and Affiliate Lenders); (G) release of any Guarantor from the Loan Guaranty (each Lender other than Defaulting and Affiliate Lenders); (H) release of all or substantially all Collateral (each Lender other than Defaulting and Affiliate Lenders); (I) changes to the Alternative Currency definition (each Revolving Lender); and (J) Lien or payment subordination of the Obligations to Senior Indebtedness, other than DIP financing, unless each adversely affected Lender is offered a bona fide pro rata opportunity to participate in the Senior Indebtedness on the same terms (excluding Ancillary Fees) with a five-Business-Day offer window. Class-specific amendments may be made by the affected Class alone. No Lender consent (other than the Administrative Agent's) is required to enter into or amend an Applicable Intercreditor Agreement for the purpose of adding holders as contemplated by its terms or as expressly contemplated by it.
units.notes: Two provisions deserve emphasis: (1) the express statement that amending the financial covenants or their component definitions is a Required Lenders matter, not a 'directly affected Lender' matter - so 6.12 levels and even the EBITDA definition can be amended by a bare majority; and (2) clause (J), an anti-lender-liability-management protection requiring pro rata participation rights before priming or subordination.

units.description: Collateral and guarantor release authority: the Administrative Agent may release Liens (i) on Payment in Full with cash collateralization of Unliquidated Obligations, (ii) on property sold or disposed of in compliance with this Agreement upon a Loan Party certificate (conclusively relied on), including releasing the Loan Guaranty of a Restricted Subsidiary 100% of whose Equity Interests are sold, (iii) on expired or terminated leased property, and (iv) as required to effect remedies dispositions. Otherwise Required Lender authorization is required, except the Administrative Agent may release Liens on Collateral valued at not more than $500,000 in the aggregate per calendar year and may release Liens in connection with any permitted transaction. The Administrative Agent may also subordinate its Liens to permitted purchase money Liens or release them where the purchase money lender requires it.
units.notes: The certificate-based release in clause (ii) is the practical mechanism by which asset sales and guarantor releases occur without a Lender vote.

units.description: Yank-a-bank: if Required Lender consent is obtained but a Lender whose consent is also necessary withholds it (a 'Non-Consenting Lender'), the Borrowers may replace that Lender by causing an acceptable assignee (not an Ineligible Institution) to purchase its Loans and assume its obligations, paying accrued interest, fees, Section 2.15 and 2.17 amounts and any Section 2.16 breakage; the assignment may be effected without the replaced Lender's signature.

The Administrative Agent may, with the Borrower Representative's consent only, amend the Loan Documents to cure any ambiguity, omission, mistake, defect or inconsistency; fee letters may be amended solely by their parties.

Expenses; Indemnity; Damage Waiver: joint and several reimbursement of Administrative Agent syndication, preparation and administration expenses (one counsel per jurisdiction, plus conflicts counsel), Issuing Bank LC expenses, and enforcement/workout expenses; enumerated reimbursable categories including appraisals, insurance reviews, field examinations and Report preparation only DURING an Event of Default, plus lien search and filing fees at all times. Broad indemnity of the Administrative Agent, Arrangers, Co-Syndication Agents, Issuing Banks, Lenders and their Related Parties for Liabilities arising from the Loan Documents, Loans, Letters of Credit, Hazardous Materials, Environmental Liability, agent administration and related Proceedings, excluding those resulting from the Indemnitee's gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith or from disputes solely among Indemnitees. Lender backstop indemnity of Agent Indemnitees pro rata. Waiver of special, indirect, consequential and punitive damages and of claims arising from electronic transmission.
units.notes: Note the deliberate gating of appraisal, insurance review and field exam cost reimbursement to periods when an Event of Default exists.

units.description: Successors and Assigns: no Borrower may assign without each Lender's consent; Lender assignments require Borrower Representative consent (deemed given after ten Business Days' silence; not required for assignments to Lenders, Lender Affiliates, Approved Funds, or during a Section 7.01(a)/(b)/(h)/(i) Event of Default), Administrative Agent consent (with carve-outs), and Issuing Bank and Swingline Lender consent for revolver assignments. Minimum assignment amounts of $5,000,000 (revolver) or $1,000,000 (term), a $3,500 processing fee, Register maintenance as a non-fiduciary agent of the Borrowers, and Administrative Questionnaire delivery. Participations permitted without consent (other than to Ineligible Institutions) with retained voting except on first-proviso Section 9.02(b) matters, Participant Register requirements, and Section 2.15/2.16/2.17 benefits capped at the selling Lender's entitlement. Federal Reserve pledges permitted. 'Ineligible Institution' captures natural persons, Defaulting Lenders and their Parents, certain personal investment vehicles, any Person that would hold more than 25% of Aggregate Revolving Exposure or Commitments during an Event of Default, Loan Parties and their Affiliates (except as permitted by 9.04(f) or (g)), and Disqualified Institutions. Section 9.04(e) sets out the Disqualified Institution regime: no assignment or participation to a Person that was a Disqualified Institution on the Trade Date without Company consent; a Company right to force divestiture at the lesser of par and the price paid; loss of information, meeting and platform access; deemed proportionate voting; agreed non-voting on plans of reorganization with Section 1126(e) designation; and Administrative Agent posting of the DQ List.
units.notes: The 25% concentration limit during an Event of Default is an anti-loan-to-own feature; the deemed-proportionate-voting and Section 1126(e) designation agreement for improperly acquired Disqualified Institution positions is aggressive.

units.description: Affiliate Lenders: any Lender may assign Term Loans to an Affiliate Lender (including a Debt Fund Affiliate) only if (A) via a Dutch Auction open to all Term Lenders pro rata or as an open market purchase on a non-pro rata basis under agreed procedures; (B) no Event of Default under Section 7.01(a), (b), (h) or (i) exists or would result; (C) an Affiliate Lender Assignment and Assumption (Exhibit F) is delivered, with a three-Business-Day recording delay; (D) Affiliate Lenders other than Debt Fund Affiliates may not hold Term Loans exceeding 20% of outstanding Term Loans (the 'Affiliate Lender Cap'); (E) plan-of-reorganization votes are cast by the Administrative Agent in the same proportion as non-Affiliate Lenders, except where the plan treats the Affiliate Lender disproportionately adversely; (F) identification and continuing voting restrictions; (G) exclusion from lender-only meetings and information; (H) MNPI representation or disclosure; and (I) Loan proceeds may not fund the assignment. Affiliate Lenders may contribute purchased Term Loans to the Borrowers for cancellation, with pro rata reduction of amortization installments. Voting: Affiliate Lenders have no Required Lender vote and are deemed voted proportionally; Debt Fund Affiliates may not account for more than 25% of the Required Lenders calculation; both may vote on each-Lender or directly-affected-Lender matters and on disproportionate treatment.
units.notes: Directly relevant to LKCM Headwater Investments III, L.P., which the definitions identify by name. Determines who counts for voting - an entity-applicability question.

units.description: Loan Buybacks: a Lender may assign Term Loans to the Company, another Borrower or a Restricted Subsidiary only if (A) via a Dutch Auction open to all Term Lenders pro rata, or as an open market purchase on a non-pro rata basis with aggregate open market purchases not exceeding $20,000,000; (B) no Event of Default exists or would result; (C) the purchased Term Loans are automatically and permanently cancelled on acquisition; (D) no Loan proceeds may fund the purchase; (E) the outstanding Term Loans of that Class are reduced by par with pro rata reduction of each amortization installment; (F) MNPI representation or disclosure; (G) selling Lender acknowledgements and waivers; and (H) the purchase is not a voluntary or mandatory prepayment.
units.notes: Note the $20,000,000 aggregate cap applies only to open market (non-pro rata) purchases; Dutch Auction buybacks are uncapped. Purchased loans must be cancelled, so no debt can be warehoused at the Company.

units.description: Survival: representations, warranties and covenants survive execution and credit extensions regardless of investigation or knowledge of a Default, and continue until Payment in Full; Sections 2.15, 2.16, 2.17, 9.03 and Article VIII survive repayment and termination.

Counterparts; Integration; Effectiveness; Electronic Execution: counterpart execution; this Agreement, the Loan Documents and separate fee/Issuing Bank Sublimit letters are the entire agreement and supersede prior understandings; effectiveness on Administrative Agent receipt of counterparts subject to Section 4.01; extensive Electronic Signature and imaged-record provisions with waivers of paper-original defenses.
Severability: invalid provisions are ineffective only in the affected jurisdiction and only to the extent of the invalidity.

Right of Setoff: during a continuing Event of Default each Lender, Issuing Bank and their Affiliates may set off deposits and other obligations against the Secured Obligations owing to them, whether or not demand has been made and even if the obligations are contingent, unmatured or held at a different branch or Affiliate; a Defaulting Lender exercising setoff must remit the amounts to the Administrative Agent for Section 2.20 application and segregate them in trust pending payment.
units.notes: Setoff is one of only two exceptions to the Section 8.07(a) exclusive-agent-enforcement rule.

units.description: Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Service: the Loan Documents are governed by the internal laws of the State of Illinois (with federal law applicable to national banks); Secured Party claims against the Administrative Agent are governed by Illinois law notwithstanding other Loan Document choice-of-law; exclusive jurisdiction of U.S. federal or Illinois state courts sitting in Chicago (claims against the Administrative Agent and its Related Parties may ONLY be brought there), with venue and forum non conveniens waivers; each Canadian Loan Party irrevocably appoints the Borrower Representative as its agent for service of process and waives sovereign or other immunity.
units.notes: Illinois (not New York) governing law, notwithstanding that certain definitions reference the New York UCC.

units.description: WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL by each party for any proceeding arising out of or relating to the Loan Documents or the transactions contemplated, with the customary certifications.
Headings and the Table of Contents are for convenience only, are not part of this Agreement and are not to be taken into consideration in interpreting it.
units.notes: Relevant to the Section 5.11 discrepancy between the Table of Contents ('Reserved') and the body ('Blocking Statute Carve-Out') - the body text controls.

units.description: Confidentiality: the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank and Lenders will maintain confidentiality of Information subject to nine exceptions (affiliates and advisors; Governmental Authority and self-regulatory requests; legal compulsion; other parties to this Agreement; remedies exercise; assignees, Participants, swap counterparties and credit-risk insurers under confidentiality agreements; Borrower Representative consent; rating agencies and CUSIP bureaus; and publicly available or independently obtained information). 'Information' excludes information obtained on a non-confidential basis and league-table data. All-caps MNPI acknowledgements and a Regulatory Authority whistleblower carve-out.

Several Obligations; Nonreliance; Violation of Law: Lender obligations are several; Lenders are not relying on margin stock for repayment; and no Lender or Issuing Bank is obligated to extend credit in violation of any Requirement of Law.
USA PATRIOT Act notice that Lenders must obtain, verify and record identifying information for each Loan Party.
Disclosure: acknowledgement that the Administrative Agent and its Affiliates may hold investments in, lend to, or have other relationships with the Loan Parties and their Affiliates.

Appointment for Perfection: each Lender appoints each other Lender as its agent for perfecting Liens that can be perfected only by possession or control; a Lender obtaining such possession or control must notify the Administrative Agent and deliver or deal with the Collateral as instructed.
Interest Rate Limitation: interest and Charges are capped at the Maximum Rate, with cumulation and later recovery of amounts not payable due to the cap, plus interest at the Overnight Rate.

No Fiduciary Duty: each Credit Party acts solely as an arm's-length contractual counterparty and not as advisor, agent or fiduciary; waiver of fiduciary-duty claims; acknowledgement of the Credit Parties' broader securities and banking activities and potential conflicts, with information-walling commitments.

Marketing Consent: JPMorgan and its affiliates may use the Borrowers' name and logo in tombstones, pitchbooks and mailings to the extent approved by the Borrower Representative (approval not unreasonably withheld), revocable by written notice.

Acknowledgement and Consent to Bail-In of Affected Financial Institutions: consent to the exercise of Write-Down and Conversion Powers by the applicable Resolution Authority, including reduction, cancellation, conversion into equity or variation of liabilities.

Acknowledgement Regarding Any Supported QFCs: U.S. Special Resolution Regime transfer effectiveness and Default Rights limitations for Supported QFCs and QFC Credit Support involving Covered Entities, with definitions of Covered Entity, Default Right and QFC.

Canadian Anti-Money Laundering Legislation: acknowledgement that Lenders and the Administrative Agent may need to obtain, verify and record CAML information about the Loan Parties, their directors, signing officers and controlling persons, with an obligation to provide it promptly.

Judgment Currency: where a judgment requires conversion of a dollar obligation into another currency, the rate used is the Administrative Agent's normal purchase rate on the preceding Business Day; the obligation is discharged only to the extent dollars can be purchased on the following Business Day, with a shortfall indemnity and excess remittance.

U.S. Loan Guaranty: each U.S. Loan Guarantor (other than those delivering a separate Guaranty) is jointly and severally liable for, and as primary obligor absolutely, unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to the Secured Parties, the prompt payment when due (at maturity, on acceleration or otherwise) of the Secured Obligations plus Section 9.03 collection costs (together the 'U.S. Guaranteed Obligations'), excluding Excluded Swap Obligations of that guarantor. The guarantee survives extensions and renewals without notice and may be enforced by any branch or Affiliate of any Lender.
units.notes: Scope note: the U.S. guarantee covers all Secured Obligations, which includes obligations of the Canadian Loan Parties - U.S. credit support flows down to the Canadian silo, but not vice versa.

units.description: Canadian Loan Guaranty: each Canadian Loan Guarantor is jointly and severally liable for, and guarantees as primary obligor, the prompt payment of the CANADIAN Secured Obligations plus Section 9.03 collection costs (the 'Canadian Guaranteed Obligations'), excluding Excluded Swap Obligations. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement including this Section, NO CANADIAN LOAN PARTY GUARANTEES ANY U.S. SECURED OBLIGATIONS.
units.notes: The operative Canadian ring-fence at the guaranty level; reinforced in Sections 2.01, 5.13(b) and (e)(i), and 11.07(a). Decisive for any question about which entities support which obligations.

units.description: Guaranty of Payment: the Loan Guaranty is a guaranty of payment and not of collection; each Loan Guarantor waives any right to require the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank or Lenders first to sue any Borrower, Loan Guarantor or other Obligated Party or to enforce against collateral.

No Discharge or Diminishment: guarantor obligations are unconditional and absolute and not subject to reduction, limitation, impairment or termination for any reason other than Payment in Full of the Guaranteed Obligations, including waiver/release/compromise of the Guaranteed Obligations, changes in the existence, structure or ownership of any Obligated Party, insolvency proceedings or resulting discharges, or setoff claims; and are not affected by failure to enforce remedies, waivers or modifications, release or invalidity of security, agent action or inaction on collateral, or delay in payment.

Defenses Waived: waiver of defenses based on any Borrower's or guarantor's defenses or unenforceability of the Guaranteed Obligations, waiver of presentment, demand, protest and notice, confirmation of non-surety status, and waiver of anti-deficiency/election-of-remedies defenses arising from judicial or nonjudicial foreclosure.

Rights of Subrogation: no Loan Guarantor may assert subrogation, contribution or indemnification claims against any Obligated Party or collateral until the Loan Parties and Loan Guarantors have fully performed all obligations to the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank and Lenders.

Reinstatement; Stay of Acceleration: guarantor obligations are reinstated if any payment is rescinded, restored or returned on insolvency or otherwise; and if acceleration is stayed by insolvency of a Borrower, the accelerated amounts are nonetheless payable by the Loan Guarantors on demand.
Information: each Loan Guarantor assumes responsibility for keeping itself informed of the Borrowers' financial condition and the risks it assumes; no Secured Party has any duty to advise it.

Release of Loan Guarantors: (a) any Loan Guarantor other than a Borrower is automatically released upon a transaction permitted by this Agreement as a result of which it ceases to be a Restricted Subsidiary, provided the transaction was not entered into for the purpose of causing the release and, where required, Required Lender consent was obtained; (b) the Administrative Agent may, at the Company's request, release any non-Borrower Loan Guarantor that is no longer a Material Subsidiary, subject to the same anti-abuse and consent provisos; and (c) the Loan Guaranty terminates automatically upon Payment in Full of all Secured Obligations.
units.notes: Clause (b) is a significant release valve: a guarantor whose EBITDA or asset contribution falls below the 5% Material Subsidiary threshold can be released on the Company's request without a Lender vote, subject to the anti-abuse proviso. Section 9.02(b)(G) otherwise requires all-Lender consent for guarantor releases 'except as otherwise permitted herein'.

units.description: Taxes: guarantor payments are made without withholding unless required by law, with gross-up for Indemnified Taxes.

Maximum Liability: each Loan Guarantor's guaranteed amount is limited to the extent necessary so its obligations are not avoidable under Bankruptcy Code Section 548 or any applicable state fraudulent transfer or voidable transactions statute or common law, taking subrogation, indemnification and contribution rights into account.
units.notes: The standard fraudulent-transfer savings clause; note the Section 3.12 solvency representation is tested on a Loan-Parties-taken-as-a-whole basis.

units.description: Contribution: a Loan Guarantor making a Guarantor Payment exceeding its share based on relative 'Allocable Amounts' (fair saleable value of property less total liabilities, including a ratable share of contingent liabilities) is entitled to contribution and indemnification from the other Loan Guarantors, exercisable only after Payment in Full of the Guaranteed Obligations and termination of this Agreement; contribution rights are assets of the Loan Guarantors.

Liability Cumulative: each Loan Party's Article X guarantor liability is additional to and cumulative with all its other liabilities under the Loan Documents, without limitation as to amount, unless the other instrument provides otherwise.

Keepwell: each Qualified ECP Guarantor jointly and severally undertakes to provide funds or other support needed by each other Guarantor to honor its Swap Obligation guarantee obligations, capped at the maximum amount that would not render the undertaking voidable under fraudulent conveyance law, remaining in effect until termination of all Swap Obligations, and intended to constitute a 'keepwell, support, or other agreement' under Commodity Exchange Act Section 1a(18)(A)(v)(II).

Appointment; Nature of Relationship: the Company is appointed by each Borrower as its irrevocable contractual representative (the 'Borrower Representative') under this Agreement and each other Loan Document, and as agent to receive all Loan proceeds in the Funding Account for prompt disbursement to the appropriate Borrower (Revolving Loan disbursements limited to Availability). The Administrative Agent and Lenders have no liability for the Borrower Representative's or Borrowers' acts or omissions.

Powers: the Borrower Representative exercises only powers specifically delegated plus reasonably incidental powers, and has no implied duties to the Borrowers or obligations to the Lenders beyond those specified.
Employment of Agents: the Borrower Representative may execute its duties by or through authorized officers.

Notices: each Borrower must immediately notify the Borrower Representative of any Default or Event of Default in a communication describing it and labeled a 'notice of default'; the Borrower Representative must promptly notify the Administrative Agent and Lenders. Any notice provided to the Borrower Representative constitutes notice to each Borrower on receipt.
