units.notes: Interacts with Section 5.02(a) (Default notice, breach of which is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d)) and Section 8.02(b) (deemed agent knowledge).

units.description: Successor Borrower Representative: resignation permitted with the Administrative Agent's prior written consent, effective on appointment of a successor, with prompt notice to the Lenders.

Execution of Loan Documents: the Borrowers empower the Borrower Representative to execute and deliver the Loan Documents and all related agreements, certificates and instruments including Compliance Certificates on their behalf, and agree that its actions and exercises of power bind all Borrowers.

Joint and Several Liability: each U.S. Borrower is jointly and severally liable for ALL Secured Obligations and all Borrower agreements under the Loan Documents and is a guarantor of each other Borrower's obligations. Each CANADIAN Borrower is jointly and severally liable ONLY for the Canadian Secured Obligations and the Canadian Borrowers' agreements, and expressly not for any U.S. Secured Obligations; each Canadian Borrower guarantees only the other Canadian Borrowers' obligations.
units.notes: Third and most explicit statement of the Canadian ring-fence, this time at the co-borrower level. Any entity-applicability analysis must reflect that Canadian Borrowers bear no U.S. obligation exposure.

units.description: Direct Liability: nothing in Section 11.07 limits any Borrower's liability for Loans made directly or indirectly to it (including Loans advanced to another Borrower and re-loaned or transferred to it), LC Exposure for Letters of Credit supporting its business, and related interest, fees, expenses and Obligations, for which it is primarily liable.

Collateral Allocation Mechanism: on the CAM Exchange Date (the first date on which either a Section 7.01(h) or (i) insolvency event occurs with respect to any Borrower, or the Loans are accelerated under Section 7.02), (i) the Revolving Commitments automatically terminate as provided in Article VII; (ii) the principal of each Revolving Loan denominated in an Alternative Currency automatically converts into Dollars at the Exchange Rate calculated as of the CAM Exchange Date, and all amounts thereafter accrue and are payable in Dollars at the otherwise applicable rates; and (iii) the Revolving Lenders are automatically deemed to have made reciprocal purchases of interests in the Designated Obligations so that each Revolving Lender owns an interest equal to its CAM Percentage in each Designated Obligation. Each Revolving Lender, each participant and each Borrower consents to the CAM Exchange and agrees to execute confirming instruments, with failure to do so not affecting validity.
units.notes: Applies only to Revolving Lenders and only to the 'Designated Obligations' (principal of and interest on Revolving Loans plus commitment fees). Term Loans and Term Lenders are NOT part of the CAM. The mechanism mutualizes currency and multi-borrower exposure among Revolving Lenders on insolvency or acceleration.

units.description: After the CAM Exchange Date, each payment received by the Administrative Agent in respect of the Designated Obligations is distributed to the Revolving Lenders pro rata in accordance with their respective CAM Percentages.
units.notes: Shared-resource rule: post-exchange recoveries on the revolver are distributed on CAM Percentages rather than by original exposure.

units.description: Nothing in Article XII prohibits a Revolving Lender from assigning interests in some but not all of the Designated Obligations it holds after the CAM Exchange, provided the assignor and assignee agree on their reciprocal rights and obligations in the event of a redetermination of CAM Percentages.
units.notes: The provision refers to redetermination of CAM Percentages 'as provided in the immediately preceding paragraph', but paragraph (b) does not in fact contain a redetermination mechanic - an apparent residual cross-reference.

documentLevelNotes:
OPERATIVE STATUS: This is the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated December 18, 2025. Section 1.11 and the recitals state that it amends, supersedes and restates the April 1, 2022 Amended and Restated Credit Agreement in its entirety WITHOUT novation: existing liens, guarantees and obligations continue and are re-evidenced under this document, and all references in the pre-existing Loan Documents are deemed to refer to this Agreement. Each Loan Party expressly ratifies and reaffirms its prior lien grants. So this document is the operative facility today, but the older security agreements and guarantees remain live as modified. 

STRUCTURE VS. A TYPICAL RESTATEMENT: the facility is now a $1.1 billion package - a $400,000,000 revolver plus a NEW $700,000,000 Initial Term Loan tranche (the 2022 facility was revolver-centric; the Initial Term Loan Commitment is defined to include re-evidencing existing Term Loans). Both tranches mature December 18, 2030. Term amortization is $8,750,000 per quarter (5% per annum) beginning March 31, 2026. Incremental capacity is a flat $500,000,000 with a 50 bp MFN. There is no excess cash flow sweep; the only mandatory prepayments are for 6.05(k) asset sales (above a $20,000,000 annual threshold, with 12+6 month reinvestment rights), Unrestricted Subsidiary dispositions, casualty/condemnation, and unpermitted debt incurrence. Declined mandatory prepayments become 'Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts' that build the Available Amount. 

FINANCIAL COVENANTS (Section 6.12): minimum Interest Coverage Ratio of 2.75 to 1.00 and maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio of 4.25 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after December 31, 2025 but prior to June 30, 2027, stepping down to 4.00 to 1.00 for quarters ending on or after June 30, 2027, with up to two Material Acquisition step-ups of 0.50x for four quarters each. First test date is December 31, 2025. Both covenants are curable under Section 7.03 (two cures per four quarters, five over the term, EBITDA-additive only, no debt netting, and disregarded for pricing and all baskets). 

RING-FENCING (the most important entity-applicability feature): the credit is bifurcated into a U.S. silo and a Canadian silo. Canadian Loan Parties never guarantee or secure the U.S. Secured Obligations, and Canadian Borrowers are jointly and severally liable only for Canadian Secured Obligations. This is stated four times (Sections 2.01 final paragraph, 5.13(b)/(e)(i), 10.01(b) and 11.07(a)). U.S. credit support does flow to the Canadian silo, not the reverse. 

SHARED-RESOURCE RELATIONSHIPS worth preserving: (1) the single 15%-of-Applicable-EBITDA cap shared by Sections 6.01(b)(iii), 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b) on U.S. Loan Party exposure to non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries; (2) the single Available Amount consumed by both Section 6.04(q) investments and Section 6.08(a)(iv) Restricted Payments; (3) the Section 6.04(r) Unrestricted Subsidiary basket, which the final paragraph of 6.04 makes the exclusive, non-replenishing, non-reallocable channel for value transfer outside the credit group; and (4) the Section 2.18(b) waterfall shared with Banking Services and Swap Agreement counterparties only up to the amount last notified under Section 2.22. 

ANTI-LEAKAGE: the document has explicit anti-trapdoor architecture - the 6.04 final paragraph, the 6.05 final paragraph (material IP may not be moved to Unrestricted Subsidiaries OR to non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries), Section 5.15's designation conditions, Section 6.01(q)(ii)(A)(3) barring non-Loan-Party obligors on ratio debt, and Section 9.02(b)(J)'s pro rata participation right before any Lien or payment subordination. 

DRAFTING DEFECTS AND AMBIGUITIES OBSERVED (each flagged on the relevant unit): (a) the Table of Contents lists Section 5.11 as 'Reserved' while the body contains a substantive Blocking Statute Carve-Out; (b) Section 6.01(q)(iv) cross-references the MFN Provision as 'Section 2.09(l)' but the MFN is in Section 2.09(g); (c) Section 2.02(a) says Term Loans amortize 'as set forth in Section 2.11' but amortization is in Section 2.10(b); (d) Section 6.04(b) uses '15% of EBITDA' while its two Section 6.01 counterparts use '15% of Applicable EBITDA'; (e) Section 6.05(d) cross-references Section 6.04(j), which is reserved; (f) Section 6.05(k) refers to a Schedule 6.05 that does not appear in the executed schedule set; (g) Article XII(c) refers to a CAM Percentage redetermination mechanic 'in the immediately preceding paragraph' that does not exist; (h) the signature page misspells the Company's name as 'DISTRIBUTION SOLUTINOS GROUP, INC.'; and (i) Section 6.11's 'materially adverse to the Lenders' qualifier is placed after clause (e) with ambiguous reach back to clause (d). 

ARTICLE XII SCOPE: the Collateral Allocation Mechanism applies only to Revolving Lenders and only to 'Designated Obligations' (Revolving Loan principal and interest plus commitment fees). Term Lenders are outside the CAM. 

SCHEDULES/EXHIBITS reviewed: Commitment Schedule (twelve lenders, JPMorgan largest at $54.5M revolver / $95.5M term), Schedule 5.14 post-closing items (insurance evidence and endorsements 30 days, DACAs 60 days, possessory collateral 10 days, NXT Capital copyright release and TestEquity/Jensen Tools chain-of-title corrections 30 days), Schedule 6.01 (approximately $1.14 million of capital leases plus three acquisition indemnity escrows), Schedule 6.02 (six existing UCC/PPSA filings), Schedule 6.04 (Columbus Insurance Ltd. share and a 25% JDJ Logistical Solutions interest), Schedule 6.10 ('None'), and Exhibits A-F. Schedules 3.05, 3.06, 3.10(b), 3.13 and 3.14 are listed but their content is largely omitted or immaterial in the filed text.
